articles.title: "It's a foundation designed all around kids": How Patrick and Brittany Mahomes are raising their own children while quietly changing the lives of thousands more
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes throws touchdowns for a living. But what he and Brittany have built off the field is harder to measure and, arguably, more lasting. Si.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes throws touchdowns for a living. But what he and Brittany have built off the field is harder to measure and, arguably, more lasting. Since launching the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation in 2019, the couple has quietly grown it into one of the most active NFL-backed charities in the country. They have distributed more than 134 charitable grants, over $2.9 million in grant funding, and donated more than 140,000 meals. The 6th Annual Gala in October 2025 alone raised $1,508,000 for 27 Kansas City charities. This is not celebrity philanthropy by press release. It is personal.How did Patrick and Brittany Mahomes start their charity foundation?The foundation's origin is simpler than its scale suggests. When Mahomes announced the foundation on The Tonight Show, he said plainly: "It's a foundation that's designed all around kids. Kids from either underserved communities that don't have the same opportunities I had when I was young, or kids that are in the hospital who have chronic illnesses or have suffered major injuries. Because those kids are the ones that train harder than me by 100 times every single day."That was 2019. Six years later, the mission has not shifted. What has changed is the reach.The Boys and Girls Clubs partnership, announced in October 2023, was a turning point. The foundation committed $1.625 million over multiple years to support clubs in Greater Kansas City, Lubbock, Tyler, and Whitehouse, Texas -- communities that personally shaped both Patrick and Brittany. The connection for Brittany was not symbolic. Patrick said in the announcement: "Kids who attend a Club, like Brittany once did, are provided with the necessary tools and resources to help this generation not only thrive but lead with compassion and purpose."Brittany put it plainly herself. "This meaningful partnership will expand opportunities for kids everywhere, and the places that have positively impacted Patrick and me," she said. "We are committed to doing all we can to uplift others."That is not a talking point. Brittany grew up in those spaces. This partnership was her full circle.What programs does the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation run for children?The foundation does not operate as a check-writing operation. It runs structured programs designed to build habits, not just fund moments.Read for 15 is a virtual program encouraging children to develop a love for reading, where kids, classrooms, and parents take a 15-week pledge. Volunteer for 15 is a partnership with Youth Volunteer Corps that pushes youth aged 11 to 18 to complete 15 hours of community service.The numbers behind Volunteer for 15 are striking. According to Youth Volunteer Corps, thanks to Patrick's leadership, 2,110 young people dedicated 92,714 hours of service across 194 cities in five countries in one year alone.Then came the scholarship program in June 2025. The foundation, in partnership with Bold.org, announced three new scholarships covering Kansas City, Tyler County, and Lubbock County, awarding $10,000 to five high school seniors in each region — a total of $150,000 for the Class of 2025. Mahomes was direct about why. "Giving back to the communities that have shaped me has always been incredibly important," he said. "These scholarships are about lifting students up and showing them that their dreams are within reach."These are not one-time donations. They are investments structured to outlast any single NFL season.How much money have Patrick and Brittany Mahomes raised through their annual charity gala?The annual gala has become the foundation's flagship event, and it keeps growing. The 5th Annual Gala in 2024 raised $1,077,000 for 20 Kansas City charities, drawing over 850 supporters. One year later, that figure jumped to $1,508,000 benefiting 27 charities at the 6th Annual Gala in October 2025.After the 2024 event, Brittany posted on Instagram: "@15andmahomies just keeps getting better. Thank you to everyone who continues to show up and help us make an impact in the world."The foundation itself captured the night's meaning well. "Together, we are changing lives. Let's keep it rolling," the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation wrote.In October 2024, a Boys and Girls Club facility in Independence, Missouri was officially renamed the "15 and the Mahomies Unit," marking the first physical tribute to the foundation's long-term investment in the community. Jason Roth, President and CEO of Boys and Girls Clubs of Greater Kansas City, summed up what that investment actually means on the ground. "It's about the stability of the clubs being here every day, having a warm meal, having wonderful staff and tutors, and just a stable ground for young people to be in when they need somewhere to go," he said.A renamed building. Thousands of volunteer hours. $150,000 in scholarships. A gala that keeps breaking its own record. Patrick and Brittany Mahomes are raising three children of their own while building something for thousands of others. The scorecard off the field is becoming just as hard to argue with as the one on it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: This Season's Super Bowl Winner Will Be One Of These 7 NFL Teams
articles.summary: These teams are the elite contenders in the NFL, and seven more could surprise this season.
articles.body: The NFL is a league built on parity and the idea that, in any given season, any team can rise from the bottom of the standings and compete for a championship. The 2025 season proved this concept, with the Patriots going from AFC East bottom-feeder to Super Bowl participant. As we head into the 2026 season, every team’s fanbase is asking the same question: Why not us? It’s a nice thought. But here, in reality, stories like last year’s Pats come along maybe once or twice a decade. Typically, we can whittle down the true Super Bowl contenders with reasonable accuracy before the season even begins. And that’s what I’ll be doing here. I’ve considered the title cases for all 32 teams and narrowed them down to a group of seven that can realistically win a Lombardi Trophy next February. So let’s look at what makes these teams title contenders before examining the group of fringe contenders who just missed the cut, along with why they were left out. One of these seven teams will win the Super Bowl: 1.Los Angeles Rams The Rams were one unlucky two-point conversion away from earning home-field advantage in the playoffs, which may have been enough to get Sean McVay’s team to the Super Bowl. It would have been easy – and maybe even sensible – for the Rams to just run it back and hope for better luck. Instead, they traded for Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett, added a lockdown cornerback in Trent McDuffie, and then lured Aaron Donald out of retirement. They were already one of the favorites to hoist the Lombardi trophy before those additions. Now, they’re the clear favorites. They check all the boxes you look for in a title contender: The acquisition of Garrett commanded a lot of the offseason attention, but adding McDuffie and Jaylen Watson to the cornerback room could be the moves that propel L.A. over the championship hump. The Rams secondary could be pushed around and picked on last season. That’s not happening with two physical corners like McDuffie and Watson on the field. Even if opposing quarterbacks can stay upright long enough to get a pass off with Garrett and Donald collapsing the pocket, finding open receivers will be a challenge. More concerns exist on the offensive side of the ball, where an injury to Davante Adams or Puka Nacua could leave the team lacking in big-play ability. The offensive line is thin, as well, and reigning MVP Matthew Stafford needs all the protection he can get now that he’s entering his age-38 season. Still, this is the NFL's most talented roster that's led by one of the NFL’s best coaches in Sean McVay. This is a Super Bowl-or-bust season for Los Angeles. 2.Seattle Seahawks The defending champs took a few hits in the offseason, losing running back Kenneth Walker and a handful of second-tier starters along the defense. Other than that, this is largely the same team that won a title in February, and they’d be the title favorites once again if not for L.A.’s busy offseason. One thing we can bank on: Head coach Mike MacDonald will have his defense playing at an elite level once again. The defensive line has been the key to the unit’s success, and all of its key pieces return in 2026. The Seahawks are light at cornerback but will play with three safeties more often than not, so that’s more of a minor concern than it would be for other teams. There’s no reason to expect any falloff from this bunch. If safety/slot defender Nick Emmanwori, an All-Rookie selection a year ago, makes the leap and plays at an All-Pro level, the Seahawks' defense may even improve over last season. There are some offensive concerns with coordinator Klint Kubiak becoming the Raiders' head coach. MacDonald went outside the building to find his replacement but went back to Kyle Shanahan’s coaching tree to poach 49ers assistant Brian Fleury. Big plays powered the Seahawks' offense – and offset some of quarterback Sam Darnold’s turnover issues – so his primary task will be keeping Seattle’s explosive play rate up. If the first-time offensive coordinator can do that and help Darnold cut down on the turnovers, Seattle will be just as formidable as the loaded Rams. 3.Baltimore Ravens The Ravens have not been a well-coached team the past two seasons. If new head coach Jesse Minter can clean up penalties and coverage busts on defense, it will go a long way. And if new offensive coordinator Declan Doyle, who comes over from Ben Johnson’s staff in Chicago, can get Lamar Jackson back to his MVP form, Baltimore can regain its place among the AFC's contenders after last year’s disappointment. The defense will almost certainly be better. Minter, one of the sharpest defensive minds in the sport, got top-10 results out of a Chargers' defense with far less talent than what he’ll be working with in Baltimore. The pass rush gets two major boosts with Nnamdi Madibuike returning from injury and Trey Hendrickson joining from the rival Bengals. Depth is a concern, but if this unit is healthy and Minter lives up to the hype, this will be a championship-level defense. Jackson’s play will determine if the offense can keep up. The two-time MVP battled injuries throughout 2026 and didn’t play his best ball when he was on the field. Jackson took far too many sacks last season, but he says he wasn’t as eager to leave the pocket last season because of the injuries and vowed to run more now that he’s healthy. That should help the two-time MVP get his groove back and elevate this offense back into the top-10. 4.Buffalo Bills The 2025 Chiefs showed us that rostering an elite quarterback isn’t enough to keep a team in title contention. So, while it feels like Josh Allen is capable of carrying the Bills to a Super Bowl, only one or two things have to go wrong for them to experience their own season from hell. Buffalo has just enough quality around Allen to make this shortlist of contenders. The offensive line, which powered one of the league’s best run games a season ago, lost left guard David Edwards to free agency, but everybody else is back. Running back James Cook is primed for another monster season, and the receiving corps added the perimeter threat it so desperately needed with the trade for D.J. Moore. No more relying on Keon Coleman for downfield targets. The Bills' offense won’t change much, but with Sean McDermott out as head coach, Buffalo’s defense is getting a makeover. First-year defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard has been a favorite among football nerds for years thanks to his work in the college ranks. McDermott ran a structurally sound defense, but smart quarterbacks had no trouble picking it apart. Leonhard’s scheme will give them more to think about. 5.Denver Broncos Denver’s Super Bowl aspirations still hinge on quarterback Bo Nix. A fractured ankle robbed him of a chance to prove he could lead the Broncos to a Super Bowl, but he’ll get another crack at it with another strong roster. Denver did lose a stout run defender in John Franklin-Myers and starting safety P.J. Locke, but the defense is stacked, and the front office used the money saved from those departures to add some firepower to the passing game in the form of receiver Jaylen Waddle. Everything is in place for a Super Bowl run … if the quarterback play is sufficient. There will be a new voice in Nix’s ear this season, with head coach Sean Payton relinquishing play-calling duties to Davis Webb. The first-time offensive coordinator is just three years into his coaching career and has never called plays in a game that counts. It’s impossible to know how he’ll handle the monumental task; but even if he falters, having a Hall of Fame play-caller as a "break glass in case of emergency" option lowers the concern. 6.Philadelphia Eagles If you’re wondering how the Eagles managed to win 11 games and another NFC East title while the offense was imploding on and off the field, just look to the other side of the ball. Philadelphia’s defense finished as a top-three unit for a second year in a row and carried the team back to the playoffs. The ceiling could be even higher in 2026. The Eagles patched up the biggest hole in their defense by adding cornerback Riq Woolen to play opposite of star Quinyon Mitchell. Philly’s pass defense was solid last season but struggled to get off the field on third down. Coordinator Vic Fangio prefers man coverage in third-and-medium situations, but with Adoree Jackson or Kelee Ringo getting torched, it wasn’t an effective strategy. While Woolen isn’t an elite cover corner by any means, he is a ball-hawk who can create turnovers if teams repeatedly try him. A secondary is as strong as its weakest link, and Philly’s weakest link will be sturdier this season. On the defensive line, the Eagles are banking on development from young players like Jalyx Hunt and Nolan Smith Jr. to make up for their numerous offseason losses. They also added veteran edge rusher Jonathan Greenard, who comes over after a down season in Minnesota. If Philadelphia can get just average pass rush production from its defensive ends, this could be the NFL’s best defense, which will keep the defending NFC East champs in contention even if the offensive issues persist. 7.Houston Texans The Texans are included here solely out of respect for Demeco Ryans' defense, which would have been good enough to drag Houston’s frustrating offense through the AFC playoffs if not for C.J. Stroud picking the worst time to play his worst-ever game. The Texans quarterback averaged 4.5 yards per attempt and threw four interceptions in the season-ending loss to the Patriots. Three of those picks were thrown over a nine-play stretch that staked New England to a double-digit lead that felt insurmountable based on how the Houston offense was playing. So, why should we expect a different outcome next January? For starters, Stroud is a much better quarterback than he showed last postseason. He may not be the franchise savior he appeared to be after his rookie season, but he’s capable of producing top-10 play for long stretches. With a truly elite defense, that’s good enough to make a run. Houston also improved its offensive line, which has been the root cause of its problems over the past few seasons. And with Stroud entering his second season in coordinator Nick Caley’s offense, there should be fewer growing pains for the offense early on. If this offense can be just mediocre, the Texans should run up another double-digit season. If Stroud can avoid another postseason stinker, the ceiling is much higher. These teams could sneak into the Super Bowl — but they aren’t winning it. New England Patriots The Patriots have a better roster than they did a year ago, and new WR1 A.J. Brown is a perfect match for Drake Maye’s game. But the defense is due for regression against a tougher slate of quarterbacks than in 2025, and the offensive line remains a work in progress. Cincinnati Bengals This offense has the potential to reach some serious highs, but we’ve been saying that for years now, and Joe Burrow and Co. have yet to produce a truly elite season. While the defense has improved, it still looks like a mediocre group at best. Detroit Lions The Lions still haven’t filled the Graham Glasgow-sized hole in the middle of its offensive line and are banking on a Dolphins castoff or a rookie to hold down the fort at right tackle with Penei Sewell swinging over to the left side. Detroit needs its offensive line to return to elite status to get this team back on track for title contention. I’m not sure it can. Jacksonville Jaguars The Jaguars are an organization on the rise, but they’re still another strong offseason – and another leap from Trevor Lawrence – away from being a true title threat. If the defense avoids regression and Lawrence finds consistency, they’re capable of a deep postseason run. Even then, it’s difficult to imagine them going toe-to-toe with the NFL’s top contenders. San Francisco 49ers The roster is old and already injured. If this were Madden, and we could turn off injuries, the 49ers would have enough talent to challenge Seattle and Los Angeles in the NFC West. But we can’t, and they probably won’t. Chicago Bears Even Ben Johnson knows that the regression gods are out to get Chicago this season after riding last year’s devil magic to a divisional title and an impressive playoff run. The Bears are headed in the right direction, but progress isn’t linear, and the division will be tougher, with Detroit and Minnesota likely to improve. Kansas City Chiefs Patrick Mahomes is coming off a late-season ACL tear, and the Chiefs made no meaningful improvements to the roster outside of adding running back Kenneth Walker. It will be another uphill climb just to make the playoffs. If not for Mahomes, they’d be nowhere near this list.

articles.title: C.J. Stroud Contract Extension Deadline Revealed by GM Nick Caserio Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Houston Texans general manager Nick Caserio revealed the timeline regarding a potential contract extension for quarterback C.J. Stroud to reporters on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Houston Texans general manager Nick Caserio revealed the timeline regarding a potential contract extension for quarterback C.J. Stroud to reporters on Tuesday.

"If we don't get it figured out before the season starts, then it'll be something we address in the offseason," Caserio said.

Houston's regular season begins on Sunday, Sept. 13, when the Texans host the Buffalo Bills at 1 p.m. ET.

Stroud is under contract for two more seasons (2026-2027) after the Texans picked up their fifth-year option on his rookie deal last April.

In three NFL seasons, he's completed 63.8 percent of his passes for 10,876 yards (7.5 yards per attempt), 62 touchdowns and 25 interceptions. The former Ohio State star has also rushed for 609 yards and four scores.

Stroud's best year was his first campaign, when he won the Associated Press Offensive Rookie of the Year award and even got MVP votes (tied for eighth in the race). He helped turn around a team that went 3-13-1 the year before his arrival and led it to an AFC South championship at 10-7 overall. The Texans even won a playoff game, destroying the Cleveland Browns 45-14 in the AFC Wild Card round.

Houston won 10 games in 2024 and 12 in 2025, making the playoffs both years. However, Stroud hasn't enjoyed the same personal success. He was 25th in quarterback rating in 2024 and 17th in 2025 after finishing sixth in that category in 2023.

Stroud also finished his 2025 season poorly, throwing four interceptions and completing just 20-of-47 passes in a 28-16 loss to the New England Patriots in the AFC Divisional Round. He did, however, help the team to a 30-6 blowout victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers in the first round.

Of course, the 2026 season brings new hope and optimism for a Texans team with a great defense on paper that should, at the very least, make Houston a playoff contender. If the offense improves and Stroud returns to his 2023 form, Houston can emerge as an AFC contender.

Stroud has shown great potential and play in the past, and he's one of the reasons the Texans have enjoyed a great turnaround after a rough three-year stretch in which the team didn't win more than 4 games in a season (2020-2022). It's clear the Texans are interested in an extension based on Caserio's comments, but one can surmise it would be after this season.

ESPN's DJ Bien-Aime provided more information.

"Throughout the offseason, the Texans and Stroud's camp have had negotiations, but nothing has been imminent toward an agreement, according to league sources. To start camp on July 29, Caserio said there was a 'possibility' the team could reach a contract extension. But with the regular season now less than two weeks away, the chance of reaching a deal is gradually shrinking."

So as of now, the Texans are full steam ahead toward a crucial regular-season opener against a Bills team that should be in the mix for an AFC crown.

articles.title: Tony Romo admits to ‘over-reliance on alcohol’ after pleading no contest to impaired driving
articles.summary: Tony Romo said Tuesday that pain caused by his career as quarterback of the Dallas Cowboys led to “an over-reliance on alcohol.”
articles.body: Tony Romo said Tuesday that pain caused by his career as quarterback of the Dallas Cowboys led to “an over-reliance on alcohol.” The admission from the CBS NFL analyst was posted to Instagram after he pleaded no-contest to operating a vehicle while intoxicated. “This morning, I faced a recent personal failure by pleading no contest to a civil offense for OWI in Wisconsin,” Romo wrote. “I own this completely.” “Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain,” he said. “That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol.” Romo, 46, “performed poorly” during a July traffic stop in Milwaukee and was arrested on suspicion of operating while intoxicated. As part of his plea, Romo will have his driving privileges revoked for six months and pay a $748 fine, according to court documents. The arrest led to his prompt suspension by CBS, where he had joined the network’s top NFL broadcast booth after he retired following 13 seasons with the Cowboys. CBS elevated former NFL star defender J.J. Watt to take his place. Last month, CBS Sports president David Berson said he did not have a timeline for a potential return for Romo because “it’s an evolving situation, and therefore we’re still assessing.” Romo did hint a return is possible in his statement Tuesday, saying that he was asking for privacy “as I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS.” “As I have taught my three young sons: when you fall short, you stand up and take full responsibility,” Romo added. “This is an important first step. The harder and more important step is examining the path that brought you here and making the changes necessary to move forward. “That path requires honesty. None of this is an excuse. These are my failures, and I take that responsibility for them,” he wrote. “I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes,” Romo said. “I am deeply grateful for the support of my family, my friends, and the NFL community including players, coaches, and owners. Your encouragement has meant more to me than you know.”

articles.title: Kenneth Walker III might be exactly what Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs needed
articles.summary: The Chiefs had seen the diminishing returns of a once-great offense and faced the prospect of their star quarterback playing at less than full health. Patric...
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks' Super Bowl run last season provided the Kansas City Chiefs a glimpse into the future. It was the vision that this scarred juggernaut needed heading into an unknown offseason.

Patrick Mahomes was a month removed from ACL surgery. The Chiefs were coming off their worst season in more than a decade. Travis Kelce was mulling retirement. Rashee Rice was in hot water off the field. There was a switch at offensive coordinator.

And just when it looked like the Seahawks were giving the Chiefs a window into how to revive their greatness, the plan almost worked too well. Kenneth Walker III already had three of the Seahawks' four longest gains late in the game, well on his way to earning Super Bowl MVP, when he busted a 49-yard touchdown run.

Even after the play was called back by penalty, Chiefs general manager Brett Veach was nervous watching the game at home, firing off a text to Mahomes in the moment. Veach had been thinking about Walker as a Chiefs savior since last "November or December" but was suddenly worried the back was outpricing himself for Kansas City, one Super Bowl carry at a time.

"I said, 'He's gonna run right to another team,'" Veach told ESPN's Pat McAfee in May, "because there weren't a lot of running backs available [in free agency] ."

Walker's playoff showcase was made possible in part by the injury to Zach Charbonnet, which increased the load the Seahawks asked Walker to lift in the playoffs. He was on the field more on third downs and in the red zone. More inside runs. Walker's receiving footprint increased. He was suddenly a workhorse back again.

In Seattle's three playoff games, Walker ran for 313 yards and four scores, adding nine catches for 104 yards and crossing the century mark for scrimmage yards in all three games. It was the best three-game stretch, production-wise, since the end of Walker's rookie season.

The Chiefs had seen enough. In the opening hour of free agency, Walker had accepted the Chiefs' offer — the most the team ever had spent on a running back and a move considered out of character for head coach Andy Reid. But they'd seen the diminishing returns of a once-great offense and faced the prospect of their star quarterback playing at less than full health.

Mahomes needed another wingman. The Chiefs didn't waste time finding him.

Where Kenneth Walker III can help the Chiefs the most

The day after the Chiefs lost to the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 18, limping to a 6-11 record after a 5-3 start, Reid admitted what had long been an issue for his offense.

"You always go to your play-action game … and you look at it and you check to see what kind of reaction you're getting from the defense," Reid said in early January. "... We're not getting enough reaction out of them."

Reid added: "There wasn't enough respect there that needs to be given. So, we've got to run the ball more efficiently, especially on first or second down on those run downs in those run situations just to stay positive with that. Somewhere you'd like to have a few bigger plays in that area."

Mahomes actually hit on the issue far earlier in the season, prior to the Week 3 game against the New York Giants. "Part of football is being able to trust in the run game whenever they're in the light boxes," he said, "and force them to come down so we can throw some of the shots down the field."

The Chiefs have typically favored rotating backs under Reid, but this looks more like a one-back show than it has in a while in Kansas City. Longtime observers of the team have been surprised just how heavy a volume Walker appears to be carrying in camp sessions, and he's often the recipient of what looks like a revived screen game and a frequent red-zone option.

That wasn't always the case for Walker in Seattle, often paired with Charbonnet and resigned mostly to early-down duty. This is newer territory for Walker, as well as for the Chiefs.

"We haven't gone through a season," Reid said, "but it looks like it's a full package of a player."

Walker is 12th in the NFL in touches since entering the league in 2022, but you wouldn't call him a true workhorse in the Derrick Henry/Saquon Barkley/Josh Jacobs/Christian McCaffrey sense. You potentially can call him a workhorse by Chiefs standards, however. In the Mahomes era, Isiah Pacheco (249 touches in 2023) has been their busiest back, and Walker has twice surpassed that total in four years in Seattle.

The Chiefs' hope is that Walker's trademark cutback style will be a featured weapon in the open field but that he also can thrive as an inside runner behind their big interior offensive line.

"Stronger than an ox," Reid said of Walker. "I mean, he's put together."

Walker's arrival also can have another positive effect on Mahomes, potentially reducing his scrambling out of necessity. At times the past few seasons, it was the Chiefs' best offensive weapon, but they became too dependent on Mahomes bailing them out with his legs.

The Chiefs ranked 25th in the NFL in rushing attempts and rush yards, 21st in yards per attempt and 20th in rushing touchdowns last season, and that was with Mahomes having the best rushing totals (422 yards and five TDs in 14 games) of his career.

"I think I ran a little too much last season," Mahomes admitted at the start of camp this year.

The downward trend can be traced back to the 2023 season, when the run game first started sagging. The Chiefs won the Super Bowl that season, and they reached the title game the following season, but the problem was compounding.

Mahomes was taking on more of the share with his scrambling, averaging nearly an extra rush attempt in 2023 than he had the year before, a trend that mostly has kept up the past three seasons. He also was getting hit more frequently (an average of 68 times per season from 2023 to 2025) and taking sacks more often (5.5% sack rate) during this span, compared to an average of 55.2 hits per season and a sack rate of 3.9% his first five years starting, per Pro Football Reference.

The Chiefs actually ran the ball moderately well the first half of last season, and Mahomes had a 17-4 TD-INT ratio through eight games. But from the Buffalo loss on, the offense looked broken. The run game stalled badly and Mahomes endured the worst statistical stretch of his career from Week 9 on.

Everything hit rock bottom when Mahomes suffered his torn ACL against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 15. The Chiefs knew that it would be ambitious for Mahomes to start the 2026 season healthy and that they couldn't go on with a substandard rushing attack.

If Walker hits the 1,000-yard rushing mark this season, it would be his third time doing it. But it would be the Chiefs' first 1K back since Mahomes took over. But Walker's impact is expected to run deeper than just one statistical benchmark — and that's what he signed up for.

"Whatever they need me to do," Walker said, "that's what I'm going to do."

Mahomes' 10th season, just as every NFL season does, will bring offensive change. But this might be the most significant Chiefs evolution offensively since Tyreek Hill was traded. When asked a few weeks ago which part of the new offensive ecosystem he was most intrigued by, with change happening all around him, Mahomes settled on Walker.

"No. 9," Mahomes said. "That's all I can say."

Walker might be lifting a heavy load in practices, but he has been kept somewhat under wraps outside the St. Joseph training fields. He spoke to the media early in camp, then once a week later, and he won't speak publicly again until the week leading up to the looming Denver Broncos showdown in Week 1.

Walker also has been a bit player in the preseason, with two snaps and two carries (for 4 yards) in the second preseason game. He's not expected to suit up for the exhibition finale. Outside of practice clips, the biggest noise on Walker has been from his new teammates raving about him.

"Ken Walker is going to be a hell of a ballplayer for us, if you didn't know that already," Travis Kelce said. "He's got every trait you can possibly want at the running back position."

For Kelce, Walker offers hope of a ride off into the sunset. Though he's not announced his future plans, this has widely been speculated to be Kelce's final NFL season — and his final shot at another ring. So far, Kelce appears thrilled with Walker, who could help him do so.

"I can't say enough about him as a teammate," Kelce said. "We got an absolute superstar on and off the field."

And they'll need him right away. Kelce isn't the same player he was. Mahomes is eight months removed from a torn ACL. Rice has been cloaked in health and off-field issues. The offensive line is far from perfect. Eric Bieniemy's return as offensive coordinator brings hope, but he has endured a tragic summer.

Things might still feel unsettled in Kansas City. But the addition of Walker has been an unquestioned well of encouragement and, the Chiefs hope, a key power source this season to keep them afloat.

"If all else fails," Mahomes said, "I'll just hand it off to K9 and let him go to work."

articles.title: Giants' Abdul Carter Reacts to Odell Beckham Jr.'s New Jersey Number With LeBron James GIF
articles.summary: New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. announced on Tuesday that he's returning to his original No. 13 jersey, and no one is happier than second-year edge rusher Abdul Carter.
articles.body:
New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. announced on Tuesday that he's returning to his original No. 13 jersey, and no one is happier than second-year edge rusher Abdul Carter.

After spending training camp sharing the No. 3 with Beckham, Carter responded to the wideout's jersey switch with a gif of NBA star LeBron James famously declaring, "It's about damn time."

Beckham wore the No. 13 jersey during his first run in New York from 2014 to 2018. When he rejoined the team this offseason, the number was already occupied by wide receiver Jaylin Hyatt. However, the Giants waived Hyatt on Sunday before being re-signed to the practice squad, opening the door for Beckham to assume his old number.

Carter is coming off a solid rookie season in which he produced 43 total tackles, seven tackles for loss and four sacks. However, much more is expected of the 2025 No. 3 pick, so he will look to break out in a big way during his sophomore campaign.

If Carter becomes the star the Giants are expecting, the No. 3 jersey will become a popular collector's item in New York.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Strategy and Ideal Landing Spots for Hidden Gems in Mock Drafts
articles.summary: Just about every fantasy football guide includes some reference to various sleepers, breakouts and busts.
articles.body:
Just about every fantasy football guide includes some reference to various sleepers, breakouts and busts.

Here's what isn't included often enough: Stressing the importance of draft value in relation to all of those terms.

Sleepers only qualify as such due to the notion they are being drafted later than they should be. So, if they jump too far up the board, then the fantasy community has awakened to them and tanked that value proposition. It's the same thing with busts and breakouts. It's not that they should or shouldn't be drafted all the time, but rather that their general draft cost sits above or behind their projected production.

With the opening of the 2026 NFL season sitting just around the corner, you might have a good feel for who the hidden gems might be. So, let's go a step beyond spotlighting them and identify the round in which they should be targeted.

Jacory Croskey-Merritt, RB, Washington Commanders

Croskey-Merritt feels a little like an impossibility in the fantasy world. Like, a starting running back in what should be an ascending offense should have no business qualifying for this exercise, right?

And yet, he feels like a hidden gem that's somehow hiding in plain sight. This offense should be better with a healthy Jayden Daniels back behind the wheel, and everyone will benefit from it.

The Commanders struggled to score last season, and Croskey-Merritt still flirted with 1,000 scrimmage yards (873) and double-digit scores (eight) as a seventh-round rookie with almost zero involvement in the passing game (13 targets in 17 games). He could easily clear those thresholds now, and if newcomer Rachaad White eats up a lot of the passing-game work, so be it—those chances already weren't coming Croskey-Merritt's way.

A reshuffled running back room still features him at the top, and Washington's new zone-blocking scheme should cater to his strengths. Add him in the ninth round, and leave everyone else figuring out how an RB2 with fringe RB1 upside ever lasted that long.

Fantasy managers clearly remember the rocky parts of Murray's NFL past, like his recent injury-impacted, generally inconsistent seasons. But they have seemingly emptied their memory banks of his best days, because at this cost, his risk factors are baked into his price, but his upside absolutely is not.

Just two seasons ago, he threw for nearly 4,000 yards and 21 touchdowns while running for another 572 yards and five scores. He tallied the 10th-most fantasy points at the position.

Know what he didn't have then but will have now? Try Kevin O'Connell as a playcaller and a surrounding cast of playmakers including Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings. Oh, and the second-easiest schedule among fantasy quarterbacks, per FantasyPros.

Arrows are almost all pointing up for Murray, but his draft cost is the one outlier. If you're someone who waits to draft a quarterback, he should be a priority. While you could try risking that he'll fall into the 12th round, an 11th round selection should ensure he's on your roster and still position you for perhaps this season's biggest bargain.

De'Zhaun Stribling, WR, San Francisco 49ers

Stribling has caught a good amount of helium since San Francisco turned a few heads by making him the top selection of this year's second round. He's the one turning heads now, as his unique blend of size (6'2", 207 lbs) and speed (4.36-second 40-yard dash) carries obvious perks.

Especially in an offense orchestrated by Kyle Shanahan, who routinely puts his top playmakers in open space. The fun thing with Stribling is he looks skilled enough to both stretch the field to open up that space for others and feast on those closer catches with the right kind of long speed to turn them into big gains.

The system fit intrigued right away, but his opportunities keep looking better. Jauan Jennings exited in free agency, Ricky Pearsall is out for the season, Christian Kirk is opening the campaign on injured reserve and Mike Evans is 33 years old and already fighting an adductor injury. Oh, George Kittle is also working his way back from a torn Achilles, while Christian McCaffrey is coming off of a 450-touch season.

Early targets might have to come Stribling's way by default, and if he makes the most of them, those chances may not decrease much even with a healthier group of pass-catchers. He could be an awesome value in the ninth round, but if you feel like you have to have him on your team, then you might have to target him in the eighth.

articles.title: Packers haven't seen surveillance video in Josh Jacobs case, GM Brian Gutekunst says
articles.summary: Gutekunst is hopeful the three-time Pro Bowl running back plays this season, but he told reporters Tuesday that Green Bay will "be prepared either way."
articles.body:
Content warning: The following article contains depictions of alleged domestic violence.

Green Bay Packers general manager Brian Gutekunst said Tuesday that, while he's hopeful running back Josh Jacobs will play this season, he disclosed that the organization hasn't seen the surveillance video in Jacobs' case and that the Packers will have a contingency plan in place if the three-time Pro Bowler isn't on the field.

"We're going to let this process play out, and we'll be prepared either way," said Gutekunst , the franchise's GM since 2018.

Jacobs, 28, was put on the commissioner exempt list on Sunday , more than three months after his arrest. He was charged Thursday with misdemeanor battery and misdemeanor criminal damage to property.

The alleged incident occurred May 23 at his home. The criminal complaint, according to ESPN , states that a woman was trying to leave Jacobs' garage when he "grabbed her and threw her to the ground, and she struck her head, suffering an injury."

The Brown County district attorney in Wisconsin said the surveillance video from Jacobs' garage corroborates the alleged victims claims of what transpired, per The Athletic .

"In the appropriate times, if those things become available (the video), we'll figure that stuff out when that time comes," Gutekunst said Tuesday.

NFL spokesperson Brian McCarthy reportedly didn't divulge if the league has seen the video, according to ESPN .

"The matter remains under review of the personal conduct policy," McCarthy reportedly said. "We do not discuss details of an ongoing investigation."

When asked if the Packers could release Jacobs, Gutekunst emphasized that Green Bay is going to let the process play out "before we make any kind of those decisions."

While on the commissioner exempt list, the 2019 first-round pick can't practice or play. That said, players are permitted to take part in other activities around their team's facility.

The NFL hasn't suspended Jacobs yet. He's in his eighth season, including his third with the Packers, who signed him to a four-year, $48 million deal in March 2024.

In his absence, however long, Green Bay is expected to lean on running backs MarShawn Lloyd, Chris Brooks and Kaleb Johnson.

articles.title: Aryna Sabalenka mocks her haters with another mesh dress, NFL legends go fishing & Tua is proud of himself
articles.summary: Aryna Sabalenka doubled down on her controversial mesh dress at the U.S. Open, then smoked her opponent to begin her bid for a third-straight title.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. September! How did this happen? I swear yesterday was April. I'm glad it wasn't, though. Because man am I ready for some football and cooler weather. I'm not really a pumpkin spice latte kind of gal — more like a walk-outside-without-my-skin-melting-and-being-swarmed-by-mosquitos kind of gal. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK I got a little taste of fall this weekend. I spent a few days in upstate New York on the St. Lawrence River, and WOW. Where has this beautiful place been hiding all my life? Look, I live in the South, so traveling damn near to Canada is a bit of a haul. So forgive my ignorance. I was up there to cover the Bassmaster Elite tournament and the Randy Moss Pro Football Hall of Fame Pro-Am. What a hoot that was — eight Hall of Famers paired with professional anglers and competing for the biggest bass. Heading into it, Randy was awfully confident in his chances to take home the trophy. In case you didn't know, he's an avid outdoorsman and even has his own bass fishing YouTube channel. On the docks, I asked Randy, "If you don't win this thing, are they going to have to rename the tournament next year?" I was obviously joking, but Randy was not having it. All business, that guy. Did Randy win? Is Megatron as good at catching smallmouths as he is at catching footballs? Did Dave Robinson bag any bass after he baited his hook with Joe Thomas' Wagyu beef jerky? Guess you'll have to read my story to find out! See how I finessed that? Anyway, if you love fishing content like this, get ready. Because now that OutKick OutDoors is officially a thing, we're going to be covering a lot more of it. Plus hunting, camping, hiking and dudes gouging out gators' eyeballs, too. TRIATHLETE WHO SURVIVED ALLIGATOR ATTACK TELLS HARROWING STORY OF HIS ESCAPE: 'I GOT SUPER LUCKY' Beats the heck out of 24/7, wall-to-wall WNBA coverage, don't ya think? Now, let's get to some Nightcaps, shall we? Aryna Sabalenka isn't giving up the mesh Remember when the tennis fashion police threw a certified hissy fit over Aryna Sabalenka's black mesh kit? The World No. 1 wore the see-through Nike dress over a bright orange sports bra and shorts during mixed doubles at the U.S. Open, and judging by people's reactions, she might as well have walked into Arthur Ashe Stadium wearing a Hefty bag. To jog your memory: Sabalenka was unfazed by the haters. So unfazed, in fact, that she showed up for her first singles match Monday wearing an orange version of essentially the same mesh getup. And then she went out and smoked Camila Osorio, 6-2, 6-4, to begin her bid for a third-straight U.S. Open title. Our fishnet queen. Aryna's been on a content heater since she arrived in New York, by the way. Painting the town, as they say. Back to the mesh kit... turns out Nike gave Aryna separate day and night kits — orange for the daytime, black for night. And they're paying her a lot of money to wear them. So maybe just relax, fashion snobs, and have yourself one of those honey deuce cocktails. A few of those and mesh starts looking good on everybody. Tua Tagovailoa is very proud of Tua Tagovailoa The world's most concussed quarterback has a new home in Atlanta, and he seems happy to be there. With just a little over a week until NFL Kickoff (thank God), Tua Tagovailoa posted a photo carousel on his Instagram account. They're all pictures of the QB in his new Falcons digs. "For the A 🫡," he wrote. Unfortunately for Tua, he also wrote something else: "We're so proud of you!! You got this ❤️" Oh nooooo, Tua! The comment was quickly deleted but not before the entire internet got the screenshot. Some have speculated that he might have meant to switch over to his wife's account, as she typically replies to his posts with some sort of "we're proud of you" message. But that's still a weird thing to do. Unless he and his wife share a phone. Like one of those boomer couples who share a Facebook account. Now, let me let you in on a little industry secret: a lot of professional athletes don't run their own social media. I know this because it used to be my job to run athletes' social media accounts for them. Keep that in mind before you hop in the DMs with some hateful nonsense. Or some nudes. (Trust me, I've seen it all.) Tua has said before that he's not on social media. So what likely happened here is that his wife runs his accounts. She probably posted the photos then forgot to switch back to her account to leave her sweet little comment. Embarrassing, but it happens. Anyway, don't worry, Tua, this Instagram snafu will all blow over, and everyone will forget about it next week — when you throw that famous fourth quarter death pick to seal the loss to the Steelers. Trust me, guys. I'm a Dolphins fan, and I've seen this movie before. I'm on a plane home to Nashville and the WiFi connection is abysmal. But shoot me your thoughts on Sabalenka, Tua, bass fishing or life in general, and we'll catch up next week.

articles.title: Stan Kroenke net worth 2026: How the Rams owner built a $24,300,000,000 empire before buying the Angels
articles.summary: NFL News: Stan Kroenke is adding another major trophy to his already enormous sports portfolio. The billionaire owner of the Los Angeles Rams has agreed to acqu.
articles.body: Stan Kroenke is adding another major trophy to his already enormous sports portfolio. The billionaire owner of the Los Angeles Rams has agreed to acquire a controlling interest in the Los Angeles Angels from Arte Moreno, bringing Major League Baseball into a sports empire that already stretches across the NFL, NBA, NHL, MLS and the English Premier League. The deal is not yet complete. Kroenke Sports & Entertainment is expected to close the transaction in the first quarter of 2027, subject to Major League Baseball approval and other closing conditions. The purchase price has not been officially disclosed.But the Angels deal has put one question back in the spotlight: just how rich is Stan Kroenke?Stan Kroenke net worth: Inside the $24.3B fortune behind the NFL owner’s stunning sports empireAccording to Forbes, Kroenke's real-time net worth stood at $24.3 billion as of September 1, 2026. And that fortune has allowed the 79-year-old Missouri-born businessman to build one of the most unusual sports portfolios in the world. That figure makes him one of the richest sports owners on the planet, although his wealth did not originally come from owning professional teams.Real estate was the foundation of Kroenke's fortune.Forbes describes him as a real-estate and sports mogul and says he owns roughly 60 million square feet of real estate, much of it shopping plazas located near Walmart stores. Kroenke also has an extraordinary land portfolio.The Land Report ranks him as the largest private landowner in the United States in its 2026 ranking, with approximately 2.7 million acres of ranchland spread across several states. His holdings include the historic Waggoner Ranch in Texas.So while sports have made Kroenke highly visible, real estate and land remain critical pieces of the fortune behind his empire.How did Stan Kroenke make his money?Kroenke began building his business career in real estate, eventually establishing the Kroenke Group and becoming heavily involved in commercial property development.His strategy included developing shopping centers, frequently near Walmart locations. His connection to Walmart is also personal: Kroenke is married to Ann Walton Kroenke, a member of the Walton family and daughter of Walmart co-founder James “Bud” Walton.However, Kroenke's own fortune is built primarily around his real-estate and business interests rather than being a Walmart inheritance. His real-estate portfolio has grown dramatically over the years, while his ranch holdings have expanded to millions of acres.The Waggoner Ranch alone became one of his most notable acquisitions. Kroenke purchased the historic Texas property in 2016 for $725 million. His broader ranch portfolio now makes him America's largest private landowner according to the 2026 Land Report.Then came the sports empireKroenke's transition from real-estate mogul to sports powerhouse began with the NFL. He became the controlling owner of the Rams in 2010 and later moved the franchise from St. Louis back to Los Angeles in 2016.The move was followed by one of the biggest developments of his career: SoFi Stadium and the surrounding Hollywood Park project in Inglewood. The Rams eventually won Super Bowl LVI in 2022, doing it inside their own stadium.But the Rams were only one piece of the puzzle.Through Kroenke Sports & Entertainment, his portfolio also includes the Denver Nuggets, Colorado Avalanche, Colorado Rapids, and Arsenal in the Premier League. And now the Angels are joining the group.Which sports teams does Stan Kroenke own?Kroenke's major-league portfolio now stretches across six major sports leagues once the Angels transaction is completed:Los Angeles Rams — NFLLos Angeles Angels — MLBDenver Nuggets — NBAColorado Avalanche — NHLColorado Rapids — MLSArsenal — Premier LeagueThe Angels will be Kroenke's first MLB franchise.The six-league description refers to the six major competitions represented by those teams. His sports holdings also include the Colorado Mammoth of the National Lacrosse League, meaning his wider professional-sports portfolio reaches beyond those six leagues.There is also an unusual ownership structure surrounding some of the teams. Because of NFL ownership rules, Kroenke transferred his ownership interests in the Nuggets and Avalanche to his wife, Ann Walton Kroenke, in 2015, although they remain part of the broader Kroenke Sports & Entertainment empire.Kroenke's teams have been winningThe eye-catching part of Kroenke's portfolio isn't simply its size.It is the number of championships his teams have collected.The Rams won the Super Bowl in 2022.The Colorado Avalanche won the Stanley Cup in 2022.The Denver Nuggets captured their first NBA championship in 2023.And Arsenal added another major success to Kroenke's collection in 2026, winning the Premier League. ESPN noted that four of Kroenke's teams had won championships in their respective sports within the previous five years.That gives Kroenke something very few owners can claim: a sports portfolio that has produced championship success across multiple major leagues and two continents.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Colts GM defends WR Keenan Allen after DWI arrest, say he will play in season opener: 'Give him some grace'
articles.summary: Keenan Allen was arrested on DWI charges  on Sunday morning in downtown Indianapolis.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts are standing by veteran wide receiver Keenan Allen after his arrest on Sunday , and insist he won't miss any games due to internal punishment for the incident this season. Allen was arrested Sunday morning in downtown Indianapolis on preliminary charges of DWI and DWI endangering a person.

Despite that, Allen "will play" in the Colts' season opener against the Baltimore Ravens on Sept. 13, general manager Chris Ballard confirmed Tuesday.

"I'm not going to comment on what happened, but what I'm going to tell you is good people make mistakes," Ballard said, via ESPN . "And he's a tremendous human being. Give him some grace."

Officers approached Allen's car when they noticed that it was parked in a no-parking zone around 1 a.m. on Sunday in downtown Indianapolis. After speaking with him, officers noticed signs of intoxication and arrested him. He was released Sunday afternoon, and reportedly has a court date set for Sept. 16.

While the Colts aren't going to administer any discipline, the NFL could still hit Allen with a fine or suspension. If he is convicted or pleads guilty to a criminal offense related to alcohol, that could be a violation of the league's substance abuse policy.

Allen signed a one-year deal with the Colts last month after spending nearly all of his career with the Chargers. He had 777 receiving yards and four touchdowns on 81 catches last season with the Chargers, and is 13th on the NFL's all-time catches list with 1,055. Kansas City Chiefs star Travis Kelce is the only active player in the league with more receptions.

Ballard cited Allen's history with the Chargers, and his relationship with former Colts quarterback Philip Rivers and Colts head coach Shane Steichen — who previously worked on staff with the Chargers — when backing Allen.

"Fourteen years in the league and no issues," Ballard said. "Decorated career, decorated teammate. As you know, our relationship with Philip Rivers, I know Philip holds him in extremely high regard. And [Steichen] was with him. And after you meet his mom and dad, who are just amazing people, we feel good about who he is. Unequivocally feel good about who Keenan Allen is."

articles.title: CeeDee Lamb Posts Video of Utah Retreat With Cowboys' Dak Prescott, George Pickens, More
articles.summary: CeeDee Lamb provided a closer look at a recent Utah retreat that he went on with Dallas Cowboys teammates, including Dak Prescott and George Pickens in a video posted to his YouTube channel on Tuesday.
articles.body:
CeeDee Lamb provided a closer look at a recent Utah retreat that he went on with Dallas Cowboys teammates, including Dak Prescott and George Pickens in a video posted to his YouTube channel on Tuesday.

"Three days away with the guys to reset, compete, and spend time with each other before the season gets going," Lamb wrote in the caption of the video. "Golf, workout, hoops, a few drinks, and a whole lot of competition in between. Nothing serious, just some good energy, and time away from ball with the fellas."

Prescott has made it an annual tradition to take Dallas' skill position players on a retreat before the beginning of training camp.

The Cowboys are looking to remain explosive offensively in 2026 after ranking No. 2 among all teams by averaging 391.9 total yards per game last season.

Prescott threw for 4,552 yards and 30 touchdowns compared to 10 interceptions while Pickens wrapped up a breakout year in which he amassed a career-high 1,429 receiving yards and nine touchdowns.

Although Lamb was limited to 14 games, he still caught 75 passes for 1,077 yards.

Dallas ultimately missed the playoffs with a 7-9-1 record, as it owned the worst scoring defense in the NFL after allowing 30.1 points per game.

The Cowboys will hope to take a step forward defensively following an offseason in which they traded for pass-rusher Rashan Gary and signed safety Jalen Thompson. Dallas added former Ohio State safety Caleb Downs with the No. 11 overall pick in the 2026 NFL draft as well.

The Cowboys will open their 2026 campaign against the New York Giants on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Joey Porter Jr. Addresses Steelers Contract Talks on Video Amid NFL Trade Rumors, 'It's Been Tough'
articles.summary: Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. says he feels he has coaches and players on his side amid ongoing contract negotiations with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. says he feels he has coaches and players on his side amid ongoing contract negotiations with the Pittsburgh Steelers.

"It's been tough, I'm not gonna lie," Porter said Tuesday (h/t ESPN's Brooke Pryor). "It's my first go around this, but it's been also great because I have all my guys with me, all the coaches and players really on my side that understand everything about the business side of things."

The Steelers earlier this week activated Porter from the PUP list, on which he has been with a back injury since July amid his bid for an extension of his rookie contract.

Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said Porter would "definitely" practice Tuesday, per The Athletic's Mike DeFabo .

Porter said Tuesday his back issues were the "whole reason" he had not been participating in practice, per Tim Benz of the Tribune-Review.

He said he "can't speak much to the future" when asked if he would be healthy in time for Week 1, per Steelers Now's Alan Saunders .

McCarthy said last week the Steelers were at an "impasse" in negotiations with Porter, who plays a position for which the top of the market was recently been recently reset by the $33 million in average annual salary the Seattle Seahawks are paying Devon Witherspoon.

Porter is currently set to play next season under a $4.9 million cap hit in the final year of his rookie deal.

The Steelers typically do not negotiate contracts during the season. General manager Omar Khan confirmed Monday that practice would remain true with Porter.

"Joey knows how we feel about him, and I still hope Joey finishes his career here," Khan said Monday.

Porter did not give a definitive answer Tuesday if he would still play in 2026 should he and the Steelers not finalize a new deal by the Week 1 deadline.

"I don't know. I have to talk to the guys upstairs, my agents, about that one," Porter said when asked if he would play Week 1, per Pryor.

When asked at a different point if he would play if healthy, per DeFabo, Porter said, "Yeah, for sure. Maybe."

The Steelers have less than two weeks before opening the regular season with a Sunday, Sept. 13 home game against the Atlanta Falcons.

Not working out a new contract by that date risks the possibility Porter could launch a holdout that would leave the Steelers to start the season without one of their most effective pass defenders.

articles.title: Isiah Pacheco Injury Update, Latest News on Lions RB's Status Ahead of 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions will be relying on starting running back Jahmyr Gibbs more than ever to start the 2026 season.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions will be relying on starting running back Jahmyr Gibbs more than ever to start the 2026 season.

The Lions announced on Tuesday that backup running back Isiah Pacheco has been placed on injured reserve, ruling him out for at least the first four games of the season. ESPN's Adam Schefter reported Pacheco is dealing with a back injury.

Pacheco signed a one-year deal with Detroit in March after spending the first four years of his career with the Kansas City Chiefs, with whom he won two Super Bowls. His signing came after the Lions traded veteran running back David Montgomery to the Houston Texans, breaking up the "Sonic and Knuckles" tandem between him and Gibbs.

A seventh-round pick in the 2022 NFL draft, Pacheco showed promise early in his career with over 1,700 rushing yards across his first two seasons. He suffered a fractured fibula early in the 2024 season and hasn't been the same since, finishing the 2025 campaign with 118 carries for 462 yards and one touchdown.

Still, the Lions were hoping that a healthy Pacheco would be able to take the load off of Gibbs, who is already one of the top workhorse running backs in the league. Gibbs signed a three-year contract extension worth up to $75.5 million last month, making him the highest-paid running back in NFL history.

Without Pacheco available, the Lions will have Sione Vaki and Jacob Saylors spell Gibbs from time to time, but it's safe to say that the three-time Pro Bowler will be getting the lion's share of the carries to start the season.

articles.title: Ex-NFL star believes Odell Beckham Jr 'still better than most of the receivers' in NFL as he returns to Giants
articles.summary: Odell Beckham Jr. made the Giants' 53-man roster and reclaimed No. 13, but Chad Ochocinco said the real question is how Matt Nagy will use him.
articles.body: The full circle career moment for Odell Beckham Jr. truly hit its peak on Tuesday when the New York Giants announced that the 33-year-old receiver, who became a household name with the franchise over a decade ago, will be wearing the No. 13 after making the 53-man roster out of training camp. Giants fans have been hoping Beckham would show new head coach John Harbaugh and the rest of the offensive staff enough to warrant a roster spot to open the season, and even at 33 years old and seven years removed from being a Giants superstar, Beckham did just that. Beckham told reporters that Harbaugh put his arm around him and congratulated him on making the team following a solid final preseason game against the New York Jets. The former first-round pick out of LSU has been through quite the career rollercoaster since he was traded to the Cleveland Browns by former GM Dave Gettleman in 2019, but he’s excited for this second chance to do what he envisioned when he was drafted in 2014: win a championship in New York. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Beckham’s return to New York has fans and peers alike celebrating with him, including former Cincinnati Bengals star wide receiver Chad Ochocinco, who told OutKick that Beckham’s movement and performance with the Giants certainly earned him a spot on an NFL 53-man roster. "I mean, there’s no scenario — I don’t care what camp he was in on any of the other 31 teams where he wouldn’t have made the team," Ochocinco said, while highlighting his partnership with DraftKings. "A healthy Odell that can create separation, that can beat any DB, that is still fast, that can take a slant route or hitch route and take it 80, 90, 70 [yards]. Whatever it may be. Odell Beckham Jr., even at 33 years old, that can still take the top off a defense? That Odell? ODELL BECKHAM JR EYES HIS OLD NUMBER AMID DRAMATIC RETURN TO THE GIANTS "I don’t need him to be the Odell of old that was with the Giants when he first got there. I don’t need him to be the Odell in his prime. I need him to be the Odell that, when your opportunities come, make the most of those opportunities. Those few opportunities he does get? He can take a slant to the house. He can make people miss. He still has flashes of greatness. I don’t need him to be the old Odell. But even at 33, Odell is still better than most of the receivers in the NFL. And not your elite receivers — let’s be realistic here." The patented separation and speed that Beckham is known for was on full display throughout training camp and the Giants’ preseason games, where he had ample opportunity to prove himself in a crowded wide receivers room. But to Ochocinco’s point, the Giants are not expecting Beckham to be their top dog once more, even if he is back in his old threads wearing his old number. Malik Nabers, whom the Giants hope will be ready for Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys, is another first-round pick out of LSU who has shown flashes of greatness. He heads into his third season coming off a severe knee injury suffered in Week 4 of last year, but should be the top dog in terms of targets and catches. Ochocinco, then, is thinking about those other opportunities where Beckham is going to have to make the best of what he’s given. "Now, making an impact, it all comes down to the opportunities that he’s given. That’s what it comes down to," he explained. "Preseason’s one thing. Now, game-planning and having plays for him, that’s a completely different animal. "You have a group of receivers, all of them do something different. There’s some things they do well and there’s some things they don’t do well. Where are those opportunities and where will Odell go do what he does well? It’s not going to be like it was years ago, it’s just not. You have to understand that, especially at 33. They weed you out of the offense once you start to hit your 30s in general anyway." Ochocinco admits he has "no idea" what the Giants and their new offensive coordinator Matt Nagy have in store for Beckham. Still, the fact he made the roster says everything you need to know: Harbaugh and the Giants believe in Beckham to make an impact — whatever that may be. "They got to use him. He’s special even at 33," Ochocinco said. Come Week 1, Giants fans will dust off their own No. 13 jerseys and wear them to MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, for the return of their former mercurial superstar. Beckham, meanwhile, will be waiting for an opportunity to help his team — no longer his old team — earn a win against an NFC East foe. OCHO LOVES DRAFTKINGS GAMEDAY We’ll see how the 17-game-plus season shakes out for Beckham, but Ochocinco is simply happy because football is back, and he’s excited to impact the fan experience with DraftKings. "DraftKings Gameday," which will take place on Sept. 2, was announced on Monday with quite the activation as it celebrates the first football season with DraftKings Sports & Casino available in all 50 states. As a way to fuel fans with the return of football, DraftKings will be offering free gas, while supplies last, to passenger vehicles at select gas stations in Los Angeles, Miami, Dallas, Atlanta and Detroit. Specific locations and event times will be announced separately. "For me, I think it’s fun because who else would do something like this outside of DraftKings? articles.title: Joe Milton Eyed for Cowboys' Practice Squad After Being Waived, Stephen Jones Says
articles.summary: Although the Dallas Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, both COO/co-owner Stephen Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer expressed significant interest in having the signal-caller back in the mix via the practice squad.
articles.body:
Although the Dallas Cowboys waived quarterback Joe Milton, both COO/co-owner Stephen Jones and head coach Brian Schottenheimer expressed significant interest in having the signal-caller back in the mix via the practice squad.

Jones made his remarks on the DLLS Cowboys podcast, and Schottenheimer revealed his feelings to reporters during his Tuesday press conference.

Milton initially made the 53-man roster after cuts were announced on Sunday. However, Dallas changed course after claiming running back Emari Demercado off waivers from the Kansas City Chiefs on Monday.

Initially, the Cowboys had three quarterbacks on the 53-man roster in starter Dak Prescott, Milton and Sam Howell. Initially, it was unclear who the Cowboys would choose to be Prescott's backup.

Schottenheimer had this to say on the matter Monday, per ESPN's Todd Archer , after the Demercado signing became official (and before Milton was let go).

"We're still piecing the puzzle together, and that's where this thing is very fluid," Schottenheimer said.

However, the Cowboys chose Howell as their QB2, making a switch from 2025, when Milton was Prescott's backup. Schottenheimer explained why.

"I think when we looked at the whole body of work, we just felt like Sam had done a little bit more in terms of executing the offense in certain areas," Schottenheimer told reporters on Tuesday, per DallasCowboys.com Staff Writer Tommy Yarrish .

"To have Joe Milton back would be incredible, we'll see what happens with the claims, and then see what he wants to do. We've shown that we know how to develop him. I think him being in this system for another year would be amazing, but I also know that he should have choices. And so, we'll see what happens, but in terms of wanting [Milton] back, absolutely."

Schottenheimer also said it was a "very, very hard decision" en route to choosing Howell, who signed a one-year deal with Dallas this offseason.

Milton did quite well this preseason, completing 29-of-43 passes (67.4 percent) for 378 yards and three touchdowns. Howell impressed as well, going 27-of-40 (67.5 percent) for 314 yards, three touchdowns and one interception.

Ultimately, Howell won the battle, but the Cowboys want him back on the practice squad. They'll get that chance, as Milton went unclaimed on waivers.

Dallas opens the regular season on Sunday, Sept. 13 at the New York Giants.

articles.title: Surprise: Virginia Tech lands South Carolina transfer days before season opener
articles.summary: Hokies land a former SEC starter days before the season opener.
articles.body:
The Virginia Tech Hokies received some unexpected help ahead of Saturday's season opener against the VMI Keydets. On Tuesday, former South Carolina defensive back DQ Smith signed with the Hokies after being granted a temporary restraining order in a Louisiana court last month.

Smith played four seasons at South Carolina, finishing his time with the Gamecocks by appearing in 48 games — 45 starts — and recording 228 tackles, including 4.5 for loss, 1.5 sacks, five interceptions and 11 passes defended. The native of Columbia, South Carolina, entered the transfer portal on Aug. 23 and was tied for the team lead in tackles last season.

Smith brings plenty of experience to an already experienced secondary.

Smith joins a safety room with Quentin Reddish, Tyson Flowers, Sheldon Robinson, Sherrod Covil, and Jordan Bass. He's expected to contribute immediately, as he was at practice on Tuesday.

The Hokies could sign Smith because he never signed an NFL contract. He attended an NFL tryout with the Minnesota Vikings but was never signed. The situation is similar to former JMU linebacker Trent Hendrick, whom the Hokies pursued, but he signed with his former college coach, Bob Chesney, at UCLA.

Head coach James Franklin was recently asked about adding players who had initially had expired eligibility and said he was always open to finding ways to improve his team.

articles.title: Report: Browns sign former Cowboys' defensive end
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns have signed this former Dallas Cowboys' defensive end after clearing waivers on Tuesday morning.
articles.body:
Despite the Cleveland Browns officially cutting down the roster to 53 players on Sunday evening, general manager Andrew Berry and the front office continue to make multiple moves before Week One of the 2026-27 NFL regular season.

According to NFL insider Jeremy Fowler on Tuesday morning, the Browns have signed former Dallas Cowboys defensive end Sam Williams after clearing waivers.

Williams' potential role with the Browns

Williams, a former second-round pick in the 2022 NFL Draft, was a key rotational piece for the Cowboys ' defense over the past few seasons. Since joining the league, Williams recorded 85 tackles, 9.5 sacks, and three forced fumbles in 49 games played.

Throughout his first two seasons in Dallas, the Ole Miss product showed plenty of promise, tallying 8.5 sacks during the stretch. Unfortunately for Williams, his career would take a turn for the worse before the 2024 season after suffering a season-ending ACL and MCL tear.

His return to the field in 2025 was underwhelming -- posting 37 tackles and one sack in 17 games. And with Dallas completely overhauling the defensive line this offseason, Williams was a causality of the roster cutdown period this past week.

The addition of Williams to the 53-man roster should not come as a surprise to Browns fans. Berry and the front office have made it a point to retool the defensive end room this offseason following the trade of star Myles Garrett and Alex Wright's season-ending injury . Cleveland signed veteran Derek Barnett earlier this offseason, as the organization will likely turn to the longtime veteran and Williams to provide additional support for newly acquired defensive end Jared Verse.

However, in order for the Browns to make room for Williams, Berry cut preseason standout cornerback Michael Coats Jr. on Tuesday. The 2026 UDFA signing out of West Virginia had an incredible stretch of games during the preseason, but the Browns could sign him to the practice squad if he clears waivers .

articles.title: Arrested after golf event, Tony Romo admits 'over-reliance on alcohol'
articles.summary: The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback was arrested in July and charged with operating a vehicle while intoxicated. He broke his silence Tuesday.
articles.body:
The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and current broadcaster for the NFL on CBS was arrested on suspicion of operating a vehicle while intoxicated on July 23 in Milwaukee County, Wisconsin.

Romo had been playing in the 125th Wisconsin Amateur Championship earlier in the day before he was arrested. He finished in a tie for 73rd, well down the leaderboard, but did make time for a fan.

Romo, who played high school golf in his hometown of Burlington along with football and basketball, showed a young fan some football drills at West Bend Country Club. That caught the eye of reporter Jim Owczarski, who snapped a few photos .

Court records show that he was facing three charges stemming from that arrest : unsafe passing on the right, possessing open intoxicants and operating a vehicle while intoxicated (OWI).

On Sept. 1, Romo announced that he pleaded no contest to a civil offense and explained that he is owning his mistakes in a statement posted to his Instagram .

Court records show that Romo's plea of no contest resulted in his driving privileges being revoked for six months. He will also have to complete the "Alcohol Assessment Program," while paying a total of $834 in fines. If he fails to pay, his license suspension can be extended for up to one year.

Romo is also required to have an "ignition interlock device" installed on any vehicles that is owned, operated or registered in his name. That will remain the case for a minimum of one year after his license is reissued.

Online court documents show the unsafe passing and open intoxicant charges were both dismissed on Sept. 1.

Football has shaped nearly every meaningful part of my life. I played for more than 20 years, including 14 in the NFL with the Dallas Cowboys. After my retirement, CBS gave me the profound honor of staying close to the game through broadcasting. Playing taught me the power of relationships, the strength of a team, and the toughness to face failure head-on with honesty, resilience, and the determination to do better. This is one of those moments when I am leaning on everything football taught me. This morning, I faced a recent personal failure by pleading no contest to a civil offense for OWI in Wisconsin. I own this completely. Multiple back surgeries ended my career earlier than I expected and left me with constant, debilitating pain. That pain led to a dependence on pain medication, and my efforts to get off those medications led to an over-reliance on alcohol. As I have taught my three young sons: when you fall short, you stand up and take full responsibility. That is an important first step. The harder and more important step is examining the path that brought you here and making the changes necessary to move forward. That path requires honesty. None of this is an excuse. These are my failures, and I take responsibility for them. The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant. It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully—to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public. I am working closely with a team of doctors to address my health and make the necessary changes. I am deeply grateful for the support of my family, my friends, and the NFL community including players, coaches, and owners. Your encouragement has meant more to me than you know.
