articles.title: CB Joey Porter Jr. noncommittal when asked if he'd still play for Steelers without extension: 'I don't know'
articles.summary: Porter, a 2023 second-round pick, is in line for a lucrative new contract, but Pittsburgh has made it clear it won't continue negotiations into the regular s...
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. may be off the physically unable to perform list, but there's no guarantee right now he'll be on the field come Week 1.

Because even if his back is good to go, his contract situation could provide complications. The 2023 second-round pick is in line for a lucrative extension, and the clock is ticking on a deal being struck, considering the Steelers are adhering to their policy of not continuing negotiations into the regular season.

When asked Tuesday if he'd play without an extension, Porter shrugged.

"I don't know," he said, via ESPN's Brooke Pryor . "I got to talk to the guys upstairs and my agents about that one."

Porter is a key ingredient for Pittsburgh's defense. The son of Super Bowl-winning Steelers linebacker Joey Porter, the 26-year-old Penn State product is coming off an impressive 2025 campaign. He allowed only 29 receptions and 299 receiving yards on 60 targets, according to Pro Football Focus, which has him down for just one receiving touchdown allowed across three seasons in the league. Additionally, Porter piled up a career-high 14 passes defended last season, per Pro Football Reference.

Like New England Patriots cornerback Christian Gonzalez, Porter is due for a pay raise . The cornerback market has already been reset this offseason, with Seattle Seahawks stalwart Devon Witherspoon — the No. 5 overall pick in 2023 — receiving a four-year, $132 million contract that made him the highest-paid corner in NFL history . He leads all players at the position with an average annual value of $33 million, per Over the Cap .

Witherspoon is followed by Denzel Ward of the Cleveland Browns ($31.1 million AAV) and Trent McDuffie of the Los Angeles Rams ($31 million AAV) , both of whom also earned eye-catching extensions this offseason.

Porter said it's been "tough" navigating extension talks, which he's done most recently while nursing a back injury that he aggravated during a mobility workout on the first day of training camp, according to ESPN .

"This is my first go around this, but, I mean, it's been also great because I have all my guys with me, all the coaches and players really on my side," Porter said, via Pryor.

"I understand everything about the business side of things. So there's not really too much to go about it, but, you know, it's been a little bit tough."

He added: "At the end of the day, it is what it is."

Porter was activated off the PUP list at the roster cutdown deadline on Sunday night.

"There's definitely a process and there's an understanding of what he was going through there with the injuries," Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said Tuesday, via TribLive.com's Chris Adamski .

"There's a process that every one of these players is going through, as far as ramping up before you go full speed on the field."

That ramp-up process will be monitored; however, Pittsburgh fans will keep a close watch on Porter's contract situation, too. The Steelers open the season at home against the Atlanta Falcons on Sept. 13.

"We won't talk publicly about the negotiations per se, but Joey knows how we feel about him, and I still hope Joey finishes his career here," Pittsburgh general manager Omar Khan said on Monday, per ESPN .

articles.title: Browns HC Says He Doesn't Care If Fans Support Deshaun Watson-Shedeur Sanders QB1 Decision
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns fans may be unhappy with Deshaun Watson as the team's starting quarterback, but head coach Todd Monken doesn't particularly care.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns fans may be unhappy with Deshaun Watson as the team's starting quarterback, but head coach Todd Monken doesn't particularly care.

"Absolutely not," Monken told reporters Tuesday when discussing whether outside opinions would impact his decision. "Would I prefer that we were all on the same page? Yeah, but that has nothing to do with my decision, and it can't ever have anything to do with my decisions. My decision has to be what's best for the Browns Week One, all the way through the season, and as long as I'm the head coach here."

Monken is correct in the belief the only thing that should impact his decision-making process is what improves the Browns' chances of winning.

Still, Watson hasn't exactly done much to improve those chances since he arrived.

While the Clemson product was once one of the best quarterbacks in the league when he was with the Houston Texans, injuries and suspension have limited him to just 19 games since joining the Browns before the 2022 campaign.

He is just 9-10 in those 19 starts with 19 touchdown passes to 12 interceptions, which stands in stark contrast to his tenure with the Texans that saw him lead the league in passing yards in 2020 and make three straight Pro Bowls.

The problem for Monken and Cleveland is Shedeur Sanders doesn't exactly offer a surefire alternative.

The 2025 fifth-round pick had seven touchdown passes to 10 interceptions with an abysmal 18.9 QBR in eight appearances during his rookie campaign. He looked every bit the part of a rookie struggling to adjust to the sport's highest level, and there is no guarantee he will be any better than Watson if he does play.

For now, Watson will be the team's starter. But fans will surely start calling for Sanders if the veteran struggles out of the gate.

To hear Monken tell it, though, that won't impact who is under center for the AFC North team.

articles.title: New Aaron Donald Rumors on Status for Rams vs. 49ers After Returning from Retirement
articles.summary: Aaron Donald might miss the Los Angeles Rams' Week 1 matchup with the San Francisco 49ers after coming out of retirement, according to ESPN's Dan Graziano.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald might miss the Los Angeles Rams' Week 1 matchup with the San Francisco 49ers after coming out of retirement, according to ESPN's Dan Graziano.

"I would say based on everything I've been told, a Week 2 or 3 debut looks more likely than Week 1," Graziano reported during a Tuesday appearance on NFL Live (0:34 mark).

Graziano noted that a Week 1 appearance is "still on the table" for the star defensive tackle, though.

On Sunday, Donald signed a one-year contract to return to the Rams after initially retiring from the NFL after the 2023 season.

While the 35-year-old missed training camp before officially joining the team, he was spotted working out at Los Angeles' facilities in July. Rams general manager Les Snead also revealed that Donald "put himself through a grueling summer."

Still, Los Angeles could choose patient approach when getting the three-time Defensive Player of the Year ready for his 2026 campaign. It's also worth noting that the Rams will travel to Melbourne, Australia for their season-opener.

Donald completed individual drills in his first practice with the team since returning before having a scheduled off day on Monday.

Rams head coach Sean McVay later confirmed that Donald has a chance to miss Week 1.

"Oh, yeah, absolutely," McVay said, per ESPN's Sarah Barshop . "That could be a possibility. I wouldn't rule anything out yet.

"But what I think is really good for us is if he's able to go, great. If not, that's kind of how we've been operating as is. And guys have done an excellent job of being able to do some really cool stuff in the meantime. And so, if he's not ready and that's not what's best for him and for the team, absolutely wouldn't have him playing Australia unnecessarily."

The Rams enter their 2026 season with high expectations, as Donald was the latest addition to a squad that already added two-time Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett in a blockbuster trade with the Cleveland Browns.

Los Angeles also bolstered its secondary by trading for star cornerback Trent McDuffie in a swap with the Kansas City Chiefs.

With reigning MVP Matthew Stafford leading the way offensively, Los Angeles has its sights set on hoisting the Lombardi Trophy.

If Donald isn't ready to suit up against the 49ers in Week 1, he could debut against the New York Giants in Week 2 or the Denver Broncos in Week 3.

articles.title: Odell Beckham Jr. reclaims No. 13 with Giants after wearing No. 3 during preseason
articles.summary: Beckham will re-emerge in Week 1 with the Giants in a spot that recalls the moment he made No. 13 his own — at home against the Cowboys on "Sunday Night Foot...
articles.body:
Odell Beckham Jr. is back. So is his No. 13.

After wearing No. 3 throughout the preseason, Beckham showed up to Giants practice Tuesday sporting No. 13, the jersey number he made his own during his first stint in New York.

Beckham is back with the Giants for the first time since 2018. In that time, he's bounced around the NFL with the Browns, Rams, Ravens and Dolphins. He signed a one-year, $1.3 million deal to return to the Giants in the offseason and made the 53-man roster cut on Sunday .

Beckham had been wearing No. 3 during the preseason. His No. 13 had been claimed by wide receiver Jalin Hyatt, who'd worn the jersey with Beckham's blessing for three seasons since joining the Giants as a rookie in 2023.

But Hyatt didn't make the cut Sunday. The Giants have since re-signed him to their practice squad after he cleared waivers. But his release from the active roster made for a clean and obvious transition back to No. 13 for Beckham, who talked Monday about what wearing his old number would mean after learning that he'd made the cut.

"I think we all know what that means to me," Beckham told reporters. "And there definitely will be some conversations. I'll just say, we'll see what happens. But it would be an honor an a privilege to put that back on."

It's not clear if any negotiations were had or even necessary with Hyatt considering Hyatt's relegation to the practice squad.

However it transpired, Beckham will make his game-day return with the Giants in Week 1 in a matchup that recalls the moment he made No. 13 his own — at home on "Sunday Night Football" against the Dallas Cowboys:

That iconic catch in 2014 and three stellar seasons to start his Giants career appeared to put No. 13 on track to be retired in New York. But a devastating ankle injury in his fourth season derailed that path, and Beckham hasn't been quite the same player since.

Beckham's since played as many seasons away from the Giants (five) as he initially did with them. But his return alongside that of his No. 13 will be a welcome sight for Giants fans at MetLife Stadium under the bright lights of "Sunday Night Football" on Sept. 13.

articles.title: Travis Kelce’s $1.5 million nonprofit faces scrutiny after records show $469,000 spent on management and $446,000 on charity
articles.summary: NFL News: Earlier this year, Travis Kelce’s reputation for giving back was facing a setback after an investigation into the NFL players’ charitable foundations .
articles.body: Earlier this year, Travis Kelce’s reputation for giving back was facing a setback after an investigation into the NFL players’ charitable foundations raised questions about how some donated money was spent. Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation raised more than $1.5 million between 2021 and 2024, yet its reported charity spending was notably lower than that of several other NFL-linked organizations.Travis Kelce nonprofit spending comes under scrutinyIn January, 2026, according to federal tax records examined by The Arizona Republic, Eighty-Seven and Running reported about $1.5 million in revenue during the three-year period and roughly $1.1 million in expenses. About $446,000 was listed under charitable spending, while $469,000 was reported as management costs.That works out to about 41 cents of every dollar spent going toward charity based on the filings. Charity Navigator generally views nonprofits spending at least 70 cents of each dollar on programs as efficient, while CharityWatch uses 75 cents as a benchmark for high efficiency.The figures have drawn attention partly because of the foundation's ties to A&A Management Group. The company was co-founded by Travis Kelce’s longtime business managers, Aaron and André Eanes. Aaron Eanes also serves as the nonprofit’s executive director.Laurie Styron, executive director of CharityWatch, raised concerns about the structure after reviewing the records.“It appears to function more as an extension of the management company versus as an independent public charity,” said Laurie Styron, the executive director of CharityWatch, an independent charity watchdog group that reviewed the nonprofit’s tax filings for The Arizona Republic.“That’s not how charities work. It’s wrong.”Travis Kelce foundation says tax filings were incorrectTravis Kelce’s team disputes the picture presented by the filings. Aaron Eanes said the reported figures did not properly classify some operational expenses tied to charitable work.“Operational costs for charitable efforts were “mistakenly reported under management rather than allocated adequately to program services,” Eanes told The Republic, so the public records do not provide an accurate “indication of where the resources were truly directed.”.Eanes said the foundation has since changed its approach, adding that management fees fell sharply in 2024 and reached zero in 2025. He also said the organization plans to expand its board, bring in nonprofit advisers and improve its reporting practices.“Looking ahead, we are expanding our board of directors, bringing on advisers with nonprofit expertise, and restructuring our reporting processes to better reflect our actual program work. We are dedicated to ensuring this foundation operates at the highest standards.”The scrutiny comes as the NFL continues to highlight charitable work through the Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year program. Kelce has been nominated three times and has supported causes in both Kansas City and his hometown of Cleveland.His foundation’s reported numbers do not erase that community work, but they do highlight why financial transparency matters. For celebrity-led nonprofits, public trust depends not only on how much money is raised, but also on how clearly and responsibly that money reaches the people it is meant to help.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'So F--ked,' NFL GM Reacts to Aaron Donald's Rams Contract After Star Comes Out of Retirement
articles.summary: Aaron Donald is back for the Los Angeles Rams, and it doesn't seem like the rest of the NFL is thrilled about it.
articles.body:
Aaron Donald is back for the Los Angeles Rams, and it doesn't seem like the rest of the NFL is thrilled about it.

"This is so f--ked," one general manager told NFL insider Jordan Schultz about the situation:

It was revealed Sunday that Donald is returning to the NFC West club, ending an offseason of speculation he would do just that. ESPN's Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter reported the future Hall of Famer agreed to a one-year, $20 million deal with playoff incentives that could make it worth up to $30 million.

And that means he will team up with Myles Garrett on the same defensive line.

Donald and Garrett are both legendary players who consistently draw double teams from opposing offensive lines. However, those lines will not be able to double both of them, which means at least one will always be in a favorable pass-rushing situation.

While Donald is 35 years old and hasn't played since 2023, his track record suggests he will still be effective.

After all, his resume includes a Super Bowl title, three Defensive Player of the Year awards, eight First-Team All-Pro nods and 10 Pro Bowl selections. He led the league with 20.5 sacks in 2018, which was one of six different seasons he finished with double-digit sacks from the defensive tackle position.

Then there is Garrett, who just set the single-season record with 23 sacks during the 2025 campaign.

Blocking both figures to be a nightmare for opponents, although the San Francisco 49ers may get some respite for their opener.

"I would say based on everything I've been told, a Week 2 or 3 debut looks more likely than Week 1," ESPN's Dan Graziano reported Tuesday on NFL Live when discussing Donald's timeline (0:34 mark).

Still, even San Francisco figures to have to deal with him when they face the Rams again in Week 14.

articles.title: 13-year-old football player Caden Sorrell dies after sudden cardiac arrest during practice, family mourns tragic loss
articles.summary: NFL News: A North Carolina football community is grieving after 13-year-old Caden Sorrell died following a sudden medical emergency during practice. The Northwe.
articles.body: A North Carolina football community is grieving after 13-year-old Caden Sorrell died following a sudden medical emergency during practice. The Northwest Guilford Middle School student suffered cardiac arrest on Sunday, Aug. 30, according to his family. Despite emergency treatment and intensive efforts to save him, Sorrell’s condition became too severe. His death has left his family, teammates, classmates and school community facing an unimaginable loss.Caden Sorrell’s family shares heartbreaking detailsSorrell was attending football practice at his middle school in Greensboro when he suffered sudden cardiac arrest, according to a GoFundMe organized for his family.Emergency responders took the seventh grader to Cone Hospital, where doctors used extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, also known as ECMO. The treatment can temporarily support the heart and lungs when they are unable to function properly.Despite those efforts, Sorrell’s family said the damage was ultimately too extensive.The family described the loss as especially painful because Sorrell leaves behind his twin brother and three other siblings. His loved ones are now dealing with grief while also trying to understand how a young athlete could be lost so suddenly.His family said doctors believe an underlying genetic condition may have contributed to his death. No specific condition has been identified publicly, and his cause of death has not been officially disclosed. His four siblings are expected to undergo testing as the family seeks more information.The school community learned of Sorrell’s death on Sunday. Principal CeCe Matson shared a message of grief with families and students.“Today, our Northwest Middle School family is grieving the loss of one of our students. There are no easy words to make sense of losing a child, and our hearts are with the family, friends, classmates, and all who loved him,” school principal CeCe Matson wrote in a Facebook post.Northwest Guilford Middle School community remembers CadenFollowing Sorrell’s death, the school’s Parent Teacher Student Organization created an outdoor memorial where students, families and community members can leave flowers, messages and other tributes.The PTSO urged people to remember Sorrell and support those closest to him during the difficult days ahead.“There are no right words for a loss like this,” the PTSO wrote in part on Facebook. “We simply want our community to know that this space is there for anyone who wishes to honor and remember a very special member of our Viking family. Please continue to keep Caden Sorrell’s family and all those who loved him in your thoughts and prayers.”Matson also encouraged students and families to lean on one another as they process the tragedy.“As we grieve this loss, let us lean on one another and extend compassion to those around us. A caring heart and gentle presence can mean so much right now,” she wrote.Sorrell’s football team is scheduled to hold a vigil on Wednesday, Sept. 2. The gathering will give teammates and members of the wider community a chance to remember the young player and stand beside his family.For those who knew Sorrell, the vigil will be about more than mourning. It will be a moment to remember a 13-year-old whose life was cut tragically short and to support a family navigating an extraordinary loss.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Inspiring story on leadership: “I want them to see women in positions of power and leadership as the norm”- How Brittany Mahomes is building a legacy her children can look up to
articles.summary: NFL News: Brittany Mahomes had a clear message for the next generation when she took the stage in Kansas City this May. Speaking at CPKC Stadium, she challenged.
articles.body: Brittany Mahomes had a clear message for the next generation when she took the stage in Kansas City this May. Speaking at CPKC Stadium, she challenged the idea that women’s leadership should be treated as something unusual or inspirational. For Mahomes, the bigger goal is normalization. She wants her children to grow up seeing women own teams, lead companies and make major decisions without anyone questioning whether they belong there.Brittany Mahomes receives major honor at CPKC StadiumMahomes delivered the message on May 6, 2026, while accepting United WE’s inaugural Champion for Change Award at CPKC Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. The organization honored her for her work as an entrepreneur, investor and co-owner of the Kansas City Current, as well as her contributions to women’s professional sports.The location itself added meaning to the occasion. CPKC Stadium was built specifically for a women’s professional sports team, giving Mahomes the chance to speak about women’s leadership from a venue that represents the change she has advocated for.Rather than treating investment in women as a symbolic gesture, Mahomes described it as a smart decision.“It’s the smartest play on the board,” she said.That idea became one of the central themes of her speech. Mahomes argued that giving women greater access to leadership is not simply about representation. It can also create stronger businesses, broader opportunities and lasting cultural change.Brittany Mahomes explains why women in power should become the normThe most personal part of Mahomes’ speech came when she connected her work to her role as a mother.She spoke about the example she wants to set for her children and explained that she does not want them to grow up thinking women’s leadership is extraordinary. Instead, she wants it to feel completely ordinary.“We talk a lot about setting an example for the next generation, and as a mom, my goal isn’t for my daughters and my son to see women’s leadership as an inspiration. I want them to see women in positions of power and leadership as the norm. I want them to grow up in a world where women owning a team or a company is the standard.”The message goes beyond her own family. It reflects a broader argument about what children learn from the world around them.A young girl who repeatedly sees women leading businesses, sports organizations and major institutions is less likely to view those positions as unreachable. The same is true for boys. Normalizing female leadership can shape expectations long before young people enter the workplace.Mahomes also tied that vision to the different roles women can hold at the same time.“And I want them to know that being a mother and an athlete, an entrepreneur, or whatever they want to be, isn’t just a balancing act. It is a power move.”Brittany Mahomes reflects on the meaning of CPKC StadiumFor Mahomes, standing inside CPKC Stadium made the message even more personal.The Kansas City Current’s home has become a visible example of investment in women’s professional sports. United WE specifically highlighted Mahomes’ role in advancing women’s sports and recognized the stadium as part of the larger progress taking place in Kansas City.Mahomes acknowledged that significance during her acceptance speech.“Being here at CPKC Stadium means so much to me,” Mahomes continued. “This building alone is a powerful symbol of the incredible growth and impact our collective efforts have made for women in leadership and women’s sports.”She also reflected on what it means to be part of a generation witnessing greater access to positions that were once dominated by men.“I’m proud to be one of many women who represent the first generation to truly see what happens when women are given keys to the stadium and the boardroom,” she added.Her words carried particular significance because the Current has helped demonstrate the commercial potential of women’s sports. The team has become an increasingly prominent part of Kansas City’s sports landscape, while its stadium provides a physical reminder that women’s professional teams deserve dedicated investment and facilities.Brittany Mahomes calls for women to own the roomMahomes’ message was not simply about gaining access to spaces traditionally controlled by men. She called for women to have enough influence to shape those spaces themselves.“We are here to build real equity and create spaces where women don’t just have a seat at the table, but they own the building that the table sits in,” Mahomes said.That distinction is important. Having a seat at the table suggests inclusion. Owning the building suggests control, influence and the ability to determine who gets invited in the first place.Her comments also fit naturally with the reason United WE selected her as the first recipient of its Champion for Change Award. The organization focuses on advancing women’s economic and civic leadership, and it credited Mahomes with helping create opportunities through her work in sports, business and investment.United WE President and CEO Wendy Doyle described Mahomes as a leader using her influence to create meaningful change across industries.The recognition therefore represented more than a personal achievement for Mahomes. It placed her work within a much larger conversation about who gets to lead and what future generations should expect from women in positions of influence.Patrick Mahomes celebrates Brittany’s achievementBrittany’s husband, Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes, also celebrated the recognition publicly.After Brittany shared photographs from the event on Instagram, Patrick responded with a short but personal message.“Congrats babe! You deserve it! Love you!” Patrick wrote.Brittany later shared her own thoughts about the ceremony, describing it as an inspiring morning focused on progress and action.The moment brought together several parts of her public identity: mother, entrepreneur, investor, sports owner and advocate for women’s professional sports.Yet her speech ultimately moved beyond those labels.Her strongest point was about what comes next. Mahomes wants children to grow up without having to question whether a woman belongs in the owner’s box, the boardroom or the leadership seat.That is why her line about wanting her children to see women in positions of power as the norm resonated so strongly. It was not simply a statement about where women are today. It was a challenge to imagine a future in which their presence at the top no longer needs an explanation.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: Jalen Hurts still views his NFL rise through the lens of losing his starting job during Alabama’s title game
articles.body:
Jalen Hurts has won a Super Bowl, earned the game's MVP award and secured one of the NFL's richest quarterback contracts. The experience that continues to frame his journey happened before any of those achievements. Hurts was benched at halftime of Alabama's national championship victory over Georgia following the 2017 season. Tua Tagovailoa led the comeback, leaving Hurts to process losing his job on college football's largest stage.

During his conversation with GQ, Hurts returned to that moment as he considered the likelihood of everything he accomplished afterward.

He remained at Alabama for another season and supported Tagovailoa. When an injury forced Hurts back onto the field in the SEC championship game, he led the Crimson Tide to a comeback victory. Hurts later transferred to Oklahoma, became a Heisman Trophy finalist and played his way into the second round of the NFL draft. The Eagles did not initially select him to replace Carson Wentz. Hurts created that opportunity through preparation, patience and his ability to respond when the depth chart changed.

His career has since included two Super Bowl appearances and a championship, but the Alabama setback remains central to how he sees himself.

Hurts compared his approach to solving a difficult shot in pool:

That belief explains why disappointment rarely produces a visible emotional reaction from him. Hurts immediately begins searching for the next available solution. His career has not been defined by being benched. It's been defined by everything he's done since.

articles.title: Rams star Puka Nacua faces new abuse allegations as $150 million payday hangs in balance
articles.summary: Hallie Aiono accused Puka Nacua of abuse and neglect in a TikTok video as the NFL reviews the Los Angeles Rams star under its conduct policy.
articles.body: Puka Nacua was on track to become the NFL’s next $150 million receiver until his offseason went sideways, with new abuse allegations surfacing as the league reviews his conduct. Nacua’s ex-girlfriend and the mother of his child, Hallie Aiono, has now accused him of abuse and neglect during their four-year relationship. Aiono made the claims in a TikTok video and then took it down. "I went from loving somebody so deeply for four years, I felt it in my bones, to experiencing extreme betrayal, abuse, complete neglect from them, in what felt like it happened almost overnight," Aiono said. She said the private turmoil had taken a greater toll than their public disputes. "A lot of the things that were public affected my mental health," Aiono said. "But honestly, the things that were happening in private are what completely crushed me and altered my brain chemistry. Those parts, what people never saw or knew of, are what broke me." The latest allegations add to a disastrous offseason for the fourth-year receiver, who led the NFL with 129 catches and added 1,715 receiving yards last season. KANSAS CITY CHIEFS WIDE RECEIVER RASHEE RICE IS ON PACE FOR AN ALL-TIME FUMBLING OF THE BAG In March, Nacua was named in a civil lawsuit filed by Madison Atiabi following a chaotic New Year’s Eve party. The filing accused him of biting Atiabi’s shoulder, biting another woman’s thumb and directing an anti-Semitic slur at a guest. Nacua’s attorney, Levi McCathern, strongly denied the allegations and characterized the legal action as an extortion attempt. "Puka denies these allegations in the strongest possible terms," McCathern said. "Our office was contacted with demands of millions of dollars in exchange for not publicizing these allegations. This is not a legitimate claim. It is blackmail." NFL PUTS 'INSPIRE CHANGE' AND 'CHOOSE LOVE' ON FIELDS BUT NOT SO AGGRESSIVE ABOUT ITS DOMESTIC ABUSE ISSUES McCathern also denied the alleged slur, saying a "completely sober witness" had stated that Nacua never made the comments. He characterized the alleged biting incidents as "horseplay." Nacua voluntarily entered a Los Angeles rehabilitation facility in early March, before Atiabi’s allegations became public. His attorney said the program was intended to help him focus on his personal growth. That off-field baggage is now bleeding into Nacua’s contract talks. Nacua recently hired WIN Sports Group to negotiate a new deal, but the Rams reportedly do not expect to extend him before the season. The team appears prepared to wait for more clarity in his legal situation and evidence of sustained personal growth before handing him top-of-market money. articles.title: Caleb Williams Lost His 'Goofy' Side as Bears' Ben Johnson Praises Maturity Entering 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has taken a more businesslike approach to his third season in the NFL, according to coach Ben Johnson.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams has taken a more businesslike approach to his third season in the NFL, according to coach Ben Johnson.

"I've seen a very composed person every time he steps into the building," Johnson said, per Jason Lieser of the Chicago Sun-Times . "This guy might've had a little bit of goofy to him a year ago, and I use that term with love. Now I see a more serious player and intent every time I'm around him. His teammates feel that as well.

"He's getting to the practice field early. He's making sure his part is taken care of. He's warmed up, he's ready to go. He stays after with the guys. He's taking a lot of pride in his approach right now, and it trickles down to everyone around him. It's a great thing. He continues to grow up and he's going to be a huge leader for us this year."

For his part, Williams said he hasn't changed completely.

"I'm going to laugh, I'm going to joke, I'm going to be goofy, I'm going to have fun," he said. "But my maturity level has gone up in understanding ... what I'm doing for the organization."

Williams faced plenty of pressure entering Year 2, but now he and the Bears are experiencing a different kind of pressure.

While Chicago isn't a top Super Bowl favorite, the team isn't a scrappy underdog anymore after winning 11 games and knocking off the Green Bay Packers in the NFC Wild Card Round.

The postseason as a whole showcased why Williams was such a highly regarded prospect going back to college. He delivered some special moments.

Much of the Bears' fortunes will hinge on him taking another step forward. He had solid numbers in 2025 (3,942 passing yards and 27 touchdowns to seven interceptions), but the jury is still out on his status as an elite signal-caller. He was 13th at his position in Bleacher Report's ranking .

Williams seems to have a firm understanding of how much he's shouldering in 2026, in terms of both team success and his individual reputation.

articles.title: Bill Simmons under review by Massachusetts authorities after admitting to proxy sports betting
articles.summary: Simmons, the founder of The Ringer, said Tuesday that it was a “lesson learned” after FanDuel voided his wagers.
articles.body: Bill Simmons, the popular sports podcaster who has championed sports betting, is under review by the Massachusetts Gaming Commission after he admitted on a recent episode to using his daughter’s boyfriend to place bets for him. The commission announced the review Tuesday, two days after Simmons said on an episode of his podcast that he’d used a proxy on multiple occasions to log in to his account and make wagers in Massachusetts. Simmons, founder of The Ringer, is based in California, where sports betting is not legal. In Massachusetts, mobile and online betting is allowed. But proxy betting — having someone place bets on behalf of someone else — is illegal in Massachusetts and is not allowed by FanDuel, the sportsbook with which the wagers were issued. “The Commission is aware of the comments made on the Bill Simmons Podcast and staff are currently reviewing the matter,” an MGC spokesman said in a statement. FanDuel is the exclusive sports betting partner of The Ringer. A spokesperson for the sportsbook told NBC News it reported the matter to the MGC and voided Simmons’ bets. On the podcast episode, Simmons said there were bets “that I really wanted to get in — the UCLA overs. But Houston, the market had not shifted appropriately yet. I can’t have my daughter do it; my dad would have no idea how to do it.” But, Simmons said, he trusted his daughter’s boyfriend and allowed him to log in to his FanDuel account. “I get the code to make sure it’s me to my phone, I give him the code, he logs in. And I have all this money that I had from last year because I actually hit a bunch of futures last year. And he’s putting in bets for me,” Simmons said, adding that “it was a real bonding moment for us.” “A week later, I called him up, ran it back,” Simmons continued. “We did some more.” In a new episode released Tuesday, Simmons said he was unaware that such bets could not be made. “I talked about how I got my daughter’s boyfriend to place some bets for me in Massachusetts because I was in L.A. [I] did not know about the proxy rules,” he said. “Yeah, there are some real rules with this stuff, and they’ve ruled that not only are the bets going to be voided — and I learned my lesson.” Simmons said he thought proxy betting was allowed. “There you go, lesson learned,” he said. Simmons, a former ESPN columnist and commentator, is one of the most popular podcasters in the country. “The Bill Simmons Podcast,” as of Tuesday, ranked No. 22 overall and No. 2 in the sports category on Spotify. Spotify acquired The Ringer — a sports and pop culture website and podcast network — in 2020 for more than $200 million, according to reports.

articles.title: “No boundaries in front of you”: How Brittany Mahomes continues to inspire her kids by showing them the value of chasing dreams, staying true to yourself and finding new purpose

articles.body: Patrick Mahomes wife Brittany Mahomes wants her kids to see what chasing a dream really means. Her own soccer journey did not follow a straight line, but the sport never left her life. Now, Sterling, Bronze and Golden are growing up around the same game that shaped their mother.That connection feels especially personal with Sterling. The five-year-old has already shown an interest in soccer, giving Brittany a chance to share a sport that once formed a huge part of her own identity. For Brittany, that is more than a cute family moment. It is a chance to show her kids that dreams can change without disappearing. Brittany Mahomes wants her kids to see what comes after a setbackBrittany Mahomes explained that mindset during a Yahoo Entertainment interview published on July 14, 2026. She spoke about how motherhood changed the way she approaches her career and made her more focused on the example she sets for her children.“Being a mom changed so many things in my life and changed how I looked at so many things,” Brittany said during the Yahoo interview. She then explained that motherhood made her more intentional and motivated her to keep moving forward.“It’s made me more intentional, more purposeful and, honestly, more motivated to keep going and keep showing my kids that there are no boundaries in front of you,” Brittany said in the same interview. “You can achieve anything. You can be a part of anything that you want to.”Those words fit her own story.Brittany played four seasons as a forward at the University of Texas at Tyler. She finished college with a degree in kinesiology and later moved to Iceland in 2017 to pursue professional soccer. That chapter did not become the long playing career she once imagined.Instead, Brittany found another direction through fitness and entrepreneurship. Years later, soccer brought her back in a much bigger way.She became part of the Kansas City Current ownership group in 2020. Patrick Mahomes joined the group in 2023. The club then opened CPKC Stadium in 2024, the first stadium built specifically for a professional women's sports team.For Brittany, that journey offers a useful lesson. She did not get everything she wanted from soccer as a player. She found another way to stay close to the sport and help create opportunities for other women. Sterling is now discovering the soccer world that shaped her mom Brittany MahomesSterling's interest in soccer goes back several years. During an October 2022 appearance on The Rich Eisen Show, Kansas City Chiefs star Patrick Mahomes explained that his daughter had started kicking a soccer ball without anyone teaching her.“We didn’t even really teach Sterling how to kick a soccer ball,” Patrick said during an interview. He explained that she saw the ball, started kicking it and then began dribbling after watching players from the Kansas City Current.Patrick also said the family attended Current games and practices because Brittany owned part of the team. He added that he did not want to force Sterling into sports, but admitted it was exciting to see those tendencies appear so early.Now, Sterling gets to see much more of that world. During Brittany's July 14, 2026 Yahoo interview, Sterling joined her at CPKC Stadium while Brittany worked on a World Cup-related video project. Brittany explained that Sterling wanted to see what her mother does at work.That small moment carries more meaning because Sterling is seeing the sport from Brittany's side. She can watch her mother work around professional players, visit the Current's stadium and learn about the game Brittany once played herself.Brittany also explained during that interview why her work now carries a bigger purpose. “Everything I do now is connected to creating more opportunities and building a future that my children can be proud of.”Brittany once chased soccer as a player. The dream changed, but she kept building. Now her kids can watch that process up close. Sterling may choose soccer. She may choose something completely different. Brittany's bigger lesson remains the same: work hard, chase what matters and do not let one setback decide where your story ends.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Travis Kelce Bought $5.3M Ohio Home Before Taylor Swift Wedding Ahead of Chiefs Season
articles.summary: It has been quite the year for Travis Kelce.
articles.body:
It has been quite the year for Travis Kelce.

The Kansas City Chiefs tight end famously married pop superstar Taylor Swift this summer, which reportedly came months after he purchased a 21,000-square-foot home on a 3.5-acre property in Ohio.

Libertina Brandt and E.B. Solomont of the Wall Street Journal reported Kelce purchased the home close to Cleveland and a private airport for $5.35 million in March.

The property is on the edge of Lake Erie and was initially built around 1895, although it was extensively renovated before it was listed on the market in 2024.

The home features eight bedrooms, as well as a game room and home theater where there was originally a ballroom. What's more, the gatehouse was turned into a two-bedroom guest cottage.

Perhaps it will eventually be a post-NFL home for Kelce, who will turn 37 years old in October and is entering his 14th season in the league in 2026. He is one of the best tight ends in NFL history with a resume that includes three Super Bowl titles, four First-Team All-Pro nods and 11 Pro Bowl selections.

While he is not as effective as he was at his peak, he was still solid last season on his way to 76 catches for 851 yards and five touchdowns.

Kelce and the Chiefs start their new campaign on Sept. 14 against the Denver Broncos.

articles.title: Clemson's Dabo Swinney throws shade at Lane Kiffin, LSU over bringing in NFL players: 'It's embarrassing'
articles.summary: Dabo Swinney called the wave of NFL players joining Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers 'embarrassing' ahead of the huge Clemson college football opener.
articles.body: Well, the biggest game of week 1 of the college football season just got a little bit bigger. There have been two big storylines dominating the headlines over the past week or so: the poor attendance at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum for USC’s home opener amid atrocious conditions and the influx of NFL players returning to college football. One team in particular has been especially aggressive at bringing in athletes who've already moved on to the NFL, and it's, surprise, surprise, Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers. TEXAS TECH HEAD COACH BLASTS USC, LINCOLN RILEY, FOR POOR ATTENDANCE AT LA COLISEUM IN WEEK ZERO This decision has been controversial, to say the least. Conferences have rushed to ban it, while prominent personalities like Ohio State's Ryan Day have spoken out against it. There are lawsuits galore, including one with a scheduled court date on Thursday morning. The SEC has already reportedly debated what type of enforcement action they might, or will be allowed, to take, should LSU follow through by putting these players on the field. This debate and its outcome is important for the future of the sport and how rosters are constructed, but it could quite literally impact College Football Playoff spots. Now, not months down the road. LSU opens their season at home in Baton Rouge against the Clemson Tigers, two programs coming off disappointing seasons and looking for a return to relevance. While LSU's a substantial favorite, and has home field advantage, Clemson is a talented team with every reason to believe they can compete or pull the upset. But that task might be a bit harder if Kiffin's allowed to use those, shall we say, advanced, players. BIG TEN BANS NFL RETURNEES, PUTTING LSU AND LANE KIFFIN ON COLLISION COURSE WITH THE SEC It was already expected to be a contentious matchup, but Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney threw a bit more fuel on the fire Tuesday afternoon when addressing this new form of roster construction. "Rarely am I at a loss for words," Swinney said. "But I'm at kind of a loss of words. I would just say it's kind of embarrassing. I mean, honestly, it's just embarrassing that that's where we are. I don't blame the kids and people trying to take advantage of the system. I just think it's embarrassing where we are with college football." It's hard to view that as anything but a shot at Kiffin, saying it's "embarrassing" that this is even a topic of conversation. Obviously, it wouldn't be, if the Tigers weren't trying to bring players back from NFL rosters. Swinney brought that up too. When addressing how he's preparing his team to play LSU, he cracked a joke about scouting NFL film. COLTS GM CHRIS BALLARD RIPS NFL PLAYERS RETURNING TO COLLEGE FOOTBALL: 'STUPIDEST S--- I’VE EVER HEARD' "Been spending this last week or so studying the Browns, the Cowboys, the Saints and the Bucs trying to get ready," he quipped. "I actually got to go watch practice in early June for the Browns. So I'm probably going to get turned in for tampering, I don't know. I wish I'd have known. I'd have paid a little more attention. Yeah, it's crazy. It's hard." He wasn't done there. Swinney said he's "embarrassed" about the fact that there seems to be no guardrails around anything in college football right now. Thanks in large part to judges who are willing to rule against any type of enforcement. "That outside stuff, we just kind of — no pun intended — we just stay in our lane here at Clemson. Try to. Every now and then, someone will ram into us. But we just try and handle our business here. But it's embarrassing; it really is. We have no rules. There's no governance. It's a joke. There's zero rules. When you enforce rules, someone just goes and finds a judge to say, 'no, you can't enforce that rule.' Never did I think I'd be living in an era like this. But that's where we are," Swinney said. OUTKICK IS NOW ON THE FOX APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD It's hard to argue with him. Kiffin was ready and willing to take advantage of this ruling because he's looking for any competitive advantage, no matter how ridiculous it might be. It's unfair to the college athletes on the LSU roster, unfair to Clemson and unfair that there's so little meaningful oversight of the sport. Not that this game needed any more drama and intrigue, but Swinney’s comments illustrate how most opposing coaches and teams will feel about playing LSU this season should those players be allowed to stay with the Tigers. Still, it would be sweet revenge for Clemson if the Tigers were able to pull off the upset anyway.

articles.title: Can Shilo Sanders escape the $11.89M judgment in his security guard case? Analyst reveals why Deion Sanders’ testimony could be crucial
articles.summary: NFL News: Shilo Sanders is fighting to erase an $11.89 million judgment tied to a 2015 altercation with former school security guard John Darjean. His bankruptc.
articles.body: Shilo Sanders is fighting to erase an $11.89 million judgment tied to a 2015 altercation with former school security guard John Darjean. His bankruptcy trial began on August 31 in Denver, and the early testimony has not helped his case. Now, attention has turned to his father, Deion Sanders, who could testify remotely before the trial ends.The case does not decide whether Shilo Sanders owes the money. A Texas court already entered the $11.89 million default judgment in Darjean’s favor in 2022. Instead, the bankruptcy judge must decide whether Shilo’s actions caused a “willful and malicious” injury. That ruling will determine whether he can wipe out the debt through bankruptcy.Shilo Sanders faces a tough road after witnesses testify against himThe case goes back to September 17, 2015, when Darjean worked as a security guard at Shilo’s school in Dallas. Darjean said he tried to take Shilo Sanders phone and accused the teenager of hitting and punching him during the confrontation.Shilo’s lawyers now argue that he acted in self-defense. That argument matters because bankruptcy law does not allow someone to erase a debt tied to a willful and malicious injury.The first day of the trial, however, gave Darjean’s side some momentum. On August 31, several witnesses testified through prerecorded video. One witness said Shilo struck Darjean with an elbow before punching him twice. Another described the attack as unprovoked, while another called Shilo’s behavior “aggressive” and “volatile,” according to Mike Florio of Pro Football Talk.That puts more weight on the defense’s version of events. Shilo’s lawyers must now convince Judge Michael E. Romero that the evidence supports self-defense rather than a deliberate attack. Deion Sanders could provide key testimony in his son’s bankruptcy fightDeion Sanders could add another piece to that argument. Darjean has said he spoke with Deion by phone shortly before the confrontation and that the phone seizure happened at Deion’s direction. Deion did not witness the physical altercation, but his conversation with Darjean could matter if Shilo’s lawyers open the door to that evidence.On August 31, Deion also publicly backed his son in a video from Colorado’s practice ground. According to USA Today’s Brent Schrotenboer, Deion said, “Praying for my baby … that people see what really transpired.”Mike Florio reported that Deion could testify remotely on September 4, but only if Shilo’s lawyers open the door to testimony about why Shilo did not want to lose access to his phone.That makes the next stage of the case especially important. Judge Romero, not a jury, will decide whether Shilo’s conduct meets the “willful and malicious” standard.If the judge rules against Shilo, the $11.89 million debt will remain. If he rules in Shilo’s favor, the former Colorado safety could have a path to discharge the judgment through bankruptcy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: What’s going on with Tony Romo? Ex-Dallas Cowboys quarterback makes candid confession about “over-reliance on alcohol”
articles.summary: NFL News: Tony Romo has opened up about his personal struggle after pleading no contest to a civil OWI offense in Wisconsin. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterba.
articles.body: Tony Romo has opened up about his personal struggle after pleading no contest to a civil OWI offense in Wisconsin. The former Dallas Cowboys quarterback admitted he has been dealing with an alcohol problem, linking it to years of pain following multiple back surgeries. Romo addressed the situation publicly on Instagram, accepting responsibility for his actions and explaining how his dependence on pain medication eventually shifted toward alcohol. His statement was unusually candid for a former NFL star who has spent years in the public eye as one of football’s most recognizable broadcasters.Romo’s comments came after his July 23 arrest in Milwaukee County. The 46-year-old was facing multiple citations following a traffic stop, including operating while intoxicated, unsafe passing and possessing an open intoxicant. He has now accepted the consequences of the OWI offense while also outlining the steps he is taking to address his health. His driving privileges have been revoked for six months, and he must complete an alcohol assessment program.Tony Romo makes confession about “over-reliance on alcohol”Tony Romo’s statement focused less on the legal case and more on the personal road that led him there.The former Cowboys quarterback said multiple back surgeries ended his playing career earlier than expected and left him dealing with “constant, debilitating pain.” He explained that the pain first led to dependence on medication. His efforts to stop taking those medications eventually resulted in what he described as an “over-reliance on alcohol.”Romo did not present his history as an excuse. Instead, he accepted responsibility while explaining the circumstances behind his struggles.“As I have told my three young sons: when you fall short, you stand up and take full responsibility. That is an important first step. The harder and more important step is examining the path that brought you here and making the changes necessary to move forward.”He also said he is working closely with a team of doctors to address his health. Romo thanked his family, friends and members of the NFL community for supporting him during a difficult period.Among those offering support was Tom Brady, who joined others in responding to Romo’s Instagram post.Tony Romo pleads no contest to OWI charge, issues apologyRomo pleaded no contest to the OWI offense on Sept. 1, bringing a significant development in the legal matter that began with his July arrest.Court records show his driving privileges were revoked for six months. He was also ordered to complete an alcohol assessment program and pay $834 in fines. An ignition interlock device must be installed on vehicles owned, operated or registered in his name, with the requirement lasting for at least one year after his license is reissued.The other citations connected to the arrest were dismissed.Romo was stopped while driving southbound on Interstate 43 after reportedly being observed making an unsafe pass. According to the supplied records, he performed poorly on standard field sobriety tests. Body camera footage later showed Romo telling deputies he had been coming from a golf tournament and was heading to visit his grandparents.The arrest came after Romo had competed in the Wisconsin Amateur Championship earlier that day. He finished tied for 73rd.Romo looks ahead to health, family and CBS returnThe legal consequences are only one part of the situation for Romo. His immediate focus is now on his health and family.“The past month has been difficult, but it has also been personally significant,” Romo said. “It has required me to confront and own my mistakes fully—to the Lord, to myself, to my family, and now to the public.”He also made clear he wants privacy while working through the situation.“As I turn my attention to my health, my family, and, in time, my return to CBS, I kindly ask for privacy during this period.”Romo has been on leave from CBS since July 31. J.J. Watt is set to join Jim Nantz and Tracy Wolfson on the network’s lead NFL broadcast team during his absence.For Romo, the next chapter is less about football than it is about addressing a problem he has now acknowledged publicly and taking the steps he believes are necessary to move forward.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: NFL bounceback candidates: Jayden Daniels, Malik Nabers headline players most likely to return to form in 2026
articles.summary: Whether due to a significant injury or poor performance in 2025, here are 12 players who should have a better 2026.
articles.body:
With the amount of parity across the league — including five different Super Bowl champions in the last six seasons — a few injuries or bad weeks can quickly derail a season. But 2025 is in the rearview mirror. Another Week 1, which opens with Seahawks vs. Patriots on Sept. 9, is a new opportunity to set higher expectations.

Whether due to recovery from a significant injury, or simply just poor performance on the field in 2025, plenty of NFL stars are poised for an improved 2026 season. From superstar quarterbacks coming off season-ending injuries, to a likely future Hall of Fame wide receiver coming off a down year, there are bounceback candidates galore.

Here are 12 NFL players who are set up for a better 2026 season than they had in 2025.

It's been a tale of two much different seasons in Jayden Daniels' young NFL career. In 2024, he had one of the best rookie seasons for a quarterback ever. In 2025, injuries prevented him from finding any kind of momentum in a lost year for Washington. This coming season should be telling about which version of Daniels is here to stay.

A healthy Daniels in 2024 was the engine of the Commanders , throwing for 3,568 yards and rushing for 891 as he immediately threatened Lamar Jackson as the NFL's best dual-threat quarterback. A trip to the NFC Championship Game appeared to set a new standard for Washington, with Daniels providing real hope to a franchise that has needed some for a long while.

In Week 2 of 2025, though, Daniels suffered a knee sprain that kept him out two weeks. In his Week 5 return, he began dealing with a hamstring strain, keeping him out another game. And in Week 9, Daniels went down with a gruesome dislocated elbow injury, which he did return from, but was ultimately ruled out for the remainder of the season by Week 15.

After missing 10 games last year, health permitting, Daniels is bounce to be better in 2026. The Commanders need him at his best if they're going to be a true NFC East threat.

Kyler Murray's career trajectory since going No. 1 to the Cardinals in the 2018 NFL Draft has slowly fallen — and this offseason, it reached a new rock bottom. Murray, once named the Offensive Rookie of the Year and a Pro Bowl selection in 2020 and 2021, was released by Arizona after seven seasons after being out-played by Jacoby Brissett at points in 2025.

Fortunately for Murray, he appears to have found the perfect home for quarterbacks in need of a career revival. It won't come easily, but the Vikings have already provided an ideal scenario for Kirk Cousins, Sam Darnold and Daniel Jones to bounce back in some fashion. The blueprint is laid out for Murray to do the same in 2026.

Playing on a one-year deal, Murray should be plenty motivated — something that's been questioned in the past — to perform well in Minnesota under Kevin O'Connell. He's not looking to bounce back from injury as much as poor 2025 performance; Murray struggled to keep the Cardinals' offense flowing when on the field.

If Murray plays well this season, he may earn himself a significant payday next spring. If he doesn't, he may become a backup. The former No. 1 pick has a lot riding on his 2026 performance, but after being named in QB1 in Minnesota, Murray has the weapons and system to thrive.

Dec 14, 2025; Kansas City, Missouri, USA; Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes (15) throws a pass during the second half against the Los Angeles Chargers at GEHA Field at Arrowhead Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jay Biggerstaff-Imagn Images

The football world knows who Patrick Mahomes is when he's on the field: a winner. As he's aged, Mahomes has slowly transitioned from a flashy, big-armed star quarterback into one who will do whatever it takes to win, including using his legs. But Mahomes was asked to do a bit too much for Kansas City in 2025 — and it cost them.

Not only did the Chiefs miss the playoffs for the first time in Mahomes' time as a starter, but he suffered a torn ACL in December, adding salt to the wound. After a long offseason of recovery, Mahomes is anticipated to play for most of the 2026 season. And while recovery from a torn ACL in 2026 isn't nearly as career-defining as it once was, there will be questions for Mahomes to answer.

Will he be athletic enough to move around in the pocket or run when needed? Can he still maximize the talent within the offense, making throws that few other quarterbacks can make? It'd be unfair to expect anything but excellence from Mahomes at this point, but his return from injury makes this a critical year.

Even before his injury in 2025, Mahomes wasn't quite the same star. One way or another, the expectation is that a healthy he can bounce back from career-lows in completion percentage (62.7%), wins as the starter (6) and quarterback rating (89.6).

By no means was Saquon Barkley "bad" in 2025 — he played in 16 of 17 games, rushing for 1,140 yards and seven touchdowns. Those numbers continued to rank among the best running backs in the league. He's a bounceback candidate, however, because of how 2025 compared to 2024.

Two seasons ago, Barkley was arguably the most impactful offensive weapon in the NFL, rushing for 2,005 yards and 13 touchdowns in the regular season before helping guide the Eagles to a Super Bowl win. He was rewarded with a reworked contract, stamped as a superstar after struggling with injuries late in his Giants tenure.

There are plenty of reasons to believe Barkley will be better this fall than he was in 2025, though. With a new offensive coordinator in Philadelphia and A.J. Brown gone, there should only be more of an emphasis on his talent's in the run game — and Barkley's abilities as a receiver won't go unnoticed either. The Eagles will need him to help replace Brown's lost production.

Barkley was also abnormally inefficient in the red zone last season, scoring his fewest total touchdowns (9) in a season with at least 13 games played since 2021. Regression back to the mean would assume Barkley can find paydirt a few more times in 2026.

Barkley wasn't as invincible last year as he proved in Year 1 with the Eagles, but the signs are there for something in between those seasons in 2026.

Can you "bounce back" after a rookie season? If so, Ashton Jeanty figures to be better in Year 2. With one year of experience under his belt in Las Vegas, the former Heisman Trophy runner-up should have much better numbers in 2026, showcasing what he's capable of in the pros after an all-time season at Boise State in 2024.

Jeanty was inefficient as a rookie, averaging 3.7 yards per carry en route to 975 rushing yards and 10 total touchdowns. Notably, he did flash a real impact as a pass catcher, with half of those touchdowns coming through the air. And now, there could be a few more lanes opened within a Raiders offense that should look improved.

If there's one thing that new Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak excelled at as an offensive coordinator, it was getting the most talented players the ball. In Las Vegas, that should mean a whole lot of Brock Bowers and Jeanty this year. Kubiak's playcalling is a big plus for Jeanty's chances of better performance in his sophomore campaign.

Las Vegas' quarterback situation also figures to be better than 2025, when Geno Smith threw 17 interceptions. Naturally, Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza taking care of the ball a bit more should mean more opportunities for Jeanty.

A preseason injury scare could throw a small wrench in things, but after managing solid numbers in a weak Raiders offense as a rookie, Jeanty should continue his ascent to stardom.

Don't blame Justin Jefferson for his full-season career-lows in receptions (84), yards (1,048) and touchdowns (2) in 2025. A wide receiver can only be as good as his quarterback situation, a lesson repeatedly showcased across NFL history — and the Vikings' quarterback play in 2025 was not good.

With J.J. McCarthy completing just 57.6% of his passes with 12 interceptions in 10 games, he made Carson Wentz's 65.1% completion mark and five interceptions in five games look adequate. For a Vikings team that typically rolls out elite quarterback play one way or another, it was a significant disappointment. When Jefferson was getting the ball, he wasn't being set up to succeed.

The star wideout, undoubtedly on a Hall of Fame trajectory, is far too talented to have consecutive "down" years. Jefferson has set the bar high for his annual production, but when he's healthy and getting accurate targets, he puts up huge numbers, something that should return in 2026.

That isn't to say the Vikings' quarterback situation is drastically improved — Murray may not be perfect, and he's had issues getting his top receivers getting the ball in the past. But nearly anything is better that Minnesota's 2025 passers. Assuming he can just get the football more often, Jefferson is an easy candidate to bounce back.

Malik Nabers was a sensation in his rookie campaign, totaling 1,204 yards and seven touchdowns despite being on a Giants team that didn't perform well. Heading into 2025, the hope was that Nabers could continue leading the offense with Jaxson Dart under center, providing an elite target to a rising quarterback. Injuries prevented that from happening.

Nabers played in just four games in 2025 before a season-ending torn ACL, keeping him in recovery mode into the late offseason. With any ACL injury, there's risk of a loss of athleticism. But based on reports from Giants training camp, Nabers appears set to return to WR1 status.

Expectations are much higher for the Giants in 2026 with John Harbaugh at the helm, Dart entering Year 2 and plenty of defensive talent. If the offense is going to take a necessary step forward, though, it will need a healthy Nabers.

It's been a while since he's had the chance to showcase his talents, but Nabers should be back in conversations among the league's best wideouts.

As mentioned with Daniels, in 2025, the Commanders' offense in general struggled to live up to the bar set in 2024. Daniels' injuries were the headliners, but in reality, a number of Washington's offensive contributors couldn't stay on the field, including Terry McLaurin.

Now entering his eighth season in D.C., McLaurin posted career lows across the board last year (38 receptions, 582 yards, 3 touchdowns), a combination of his own injury issues and Daniels'. With both healthy entering 2026, one of the NFL's best red-zone connections from two seasons ago could return.

It was with Daniels at quarterback in 2024 that McLaurin set a new career-best with 13 touchdowns, looking rejuvenated after years of offensive struggles in Washington. At 31 years old, McLaurin isn't going to be an annual threat for 1,110 yards, but he can still provide plenty of stability at his position for the Commanders.

Health permitting, McLaurin should directly benefit from a healthy Daniels after struggling last year.

Another 31-year-old pass catcher in the DMV area primed for a 2026 bounce-back is the Ravens' Mark Andrews, who has long been considered one of the NFL's best all-around tight ends, yet has faded in recent years.

After dealing with injuries in 2023, Andrews' red-zone success (11 touchdowns) made him extremely valuable in 2024. But 2025 was a much different story; he finished with 422 yards, the lowest of his eight-year career.

Age certainly has played a role in Andrews' decline in production, but offseason changes in Baltimore should lead to an increase in targets for the three-time Pro Bowler. Jessie Minter appointed Declan Doyle as his offensive coordinator, a change in play-calling that could lead to an increased presence for Andrews. Additionally, Isaiah Likely — a longtime threat in the tight end room to Andrews' numbers — is gone, signing with the Giants in free agency.

Even if its just as Lamar Jackson's go-to option in the red zone, Andrews has a path to more of an active role in 2026.

The Packers will have two players returning from ACL tears at some point in 2026, and both are critical to the team's success. Tight end Tucker Kraft, who broke out in 2025 before his injury, will give Jordan Love an elite threat in the middle of the field again, while Micah Parsons will be looking to return to his dominant ways on the defensive end.

Parsons isn't exactly a "bounce back" candidate because of poor 2025 numbers. He still managed 12.5 sacks and two forced fumbles over 14 games last season prior to his injury, marking his fifth-straight season to open his career with at least 12 sacks. When he's on the field, Parsons is one of the NFL's best defenders, plain and simple.

Parsons will face the same questions as Mahomes, Kraft and Nabers, though: Will his athletic burst be the same? The assumption is yes — the 6-foot-3, 250-pound pass rusher has proven time and time again that he's a force to be reckoned with on the field.

Parsons' return should immediately make the Packers' pass rush elite again. He's one of the few players across the league who can swing games by himself.

Sep 14, 2025; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals defensive end Trey Hendrickson (91) celebrates the win after the game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Joseph Maiorana-Imagn Images

It was time for Trey Hendrickson to find a change of scenery. After five years with the Bengals, which featured three seasons of at least 14 sacks, four Pro Bowl nods, trade requests and contract holdouts, Hendrickson finally departed this offseason for the division rival Ravens.

The move also comes at a point with Hendrickson coming off a 2025 season in which he played just seven games due to injury, totaling four sacks. Baltimore forked over $112 million with the belief that Hendrickson can bounce back in 2026 and continue getting after quarterbacks, something he's consistently done for years.

Following the controversy of the failed Maxx Crosby trade and a head coaching change, there's a bit more pressure to succeed going around in Baltimore this season. Hendrickson was the prize of the Ravens' offseason. Now that he's healthy again, he should return to his status as one of the game's best pass rushers.

Rounding out the list is yet another superstar who hasn't seen the field in almost a year due to a torn ACL. From 2021-24, Nick Bosa totaled at least nine sacks in every season, winning Defensive Player of the Year in 2022 and leading the 49ers to the Super Bowl in 2024. Three games into his 2025 season, it was derailed by one of many injuries for San Francisco.

Health remains a major concern for most of the 49ers roster, but Bosa, like Parsons, produces when he's on the field. There isn't much concern that he won't be who he once was; his nearly 270-pound frame has overwhelmed many offensive lineman, and that shouldn't change after the torn ACL.

San Francisco will also need Bosa to keep up in a loaded division, as the Rams have added both Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald this offseason, on top of the defending champion Seahawks. Elite pass-rushing is a must in the NFC West, and the 49ers can only keep up in that department with Bosa.

When Week 1 rolls around, Bosa will be among the group of NFL stars set to make a highly-anticipated return to action after an ACL injury in 2025.
