articles.title: Jets news: Why Field Yates believes David Bailey will make instant impact
articles.summary: The New York Jets have had five players who were named Defensive Rookie of the Year. David Bailey is looking to add his name to the list. Bailey is hoping to...
articles.body:
The New York Jets have had five players who were named Defensive Rookie of the Year. David Bailey is looking to add his name to the list.

Bailey is hoping to join Erik McMillan in 1988, Hugh Douglas in 1995, Jonathan Vilma in 2004, Sheldon Richardson in 2013, and Sauce Gardner in 2002.

The 23-year-old defensive end will be one of the newcomers to watch in the upcoming season. It will be interesting to see whether he can live up to the hype of being the No. 2 pick and adjust to the physicality, speed, and pace of the NFL.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

ESPN's Field Yates picked Bailey as one of the five rookies who will make an immediate impact .

"The Jets did the right thing at No. 2 overall. They did not overthink it. Let's take clearly the best pass rusher in the draft. Nobody had more sacks than David Bailey in the FBS last year," said Yates.

"You just love the first-step quickness, the physicality, the heavy hands, the ability to win from a two- or three-point stance. I think David Bailey's gonna help, which should be a much-improved Jets front seven."

Bailey earned praise in training camp for his explosiveness, energy, and motor. He was compared to Richardson and Gardner , who anchored the defense of the Jets.

In his four years at Notre Dame and Texas Tech, he collected 163 combined tackles, including 42 tackles for loss, 29 sacks, four passes defended, and 10 forced fumbles. He was named a Unanimous All-American and the Big 12 Defensive Lineman of the Year in 2025.

Other rookies who can make an immediate impact, according to Yates, are Arizona Cardinals running back Jeremiyah Love, New York Giants guard Francis Mauigoa, Cleveland Browns offensive tackle Spencer Fano, and Dallas Cowboys safety Caleb Downs.

articles.title: The 5 Fantasy Football League Winners for 2026 NFL Season
articles.summary: Fantasy football seasons are shaped by league winners.
articles.body:
Fantasy football seasons are shaped by league winners.

These winners come in many forms, including first-round stars who manage to top the lofty projections set for them, the mid-round picks who go above and beyond the modest contributions expected of their draft slot and the late-round steals and free-agent scores who accomplish far more than pad out a roster's depth.

According to Tristan H. Cockcroft of ESPN, the league winners from last season included Puka Nacua (found on 29.1 percent of the site's championship teams), Jaxson Smith-Njigba (25.2 percent), Bijan Robinson (23.8 percent), Trey McBride (22.4 percent) and Christian McCaffrey (20.1 percent).

Most of these players were projected to make a major impact last year—Smith-Njigba and McBride being the only two without first-round ADPs—but Robinson was the only consensus top-five selection of the bunch. This shows how managers can find league-winning talent regardless of their starting draft slot.

Other players consistently found on winning squads included Brandon Aubrey (18.7 percent), James Cook III (18.2 percent), Drake Maye (18 percent), Michael Wilson (17.4 percent) and Chase Brown (17.1 percent).

This group highlights the importance of making shrewd decisions in the mid-to-late portions of a draft as well as in free agency, as it didn't contain a single player with an ADP better than 25—including Wilson notably going undrafted in most formats.

Having league-winning pieces on your squad will be just as important in 2026. The managers who come away from a draft with a couple of them in tow will have a major leg up over the competition, especially those who go on to scour the waiver wire and add key free agents over the next few months.

It's not easy to identify league winners, though. Injuries and other unexpected events shake up every fantasy campaign, leaving teams that looked perfectly positioned to compete for a championship in September well out of playoff contention come December.

Despite this, there are still several players who stick out for their better-than-average chances of breaking out as a 2026 league winner.

Whether they have the potential to outperform their consensus first-round peers by a wide margin or are a projected late-rounder with sneaky top-10 upside, these talents should be atop your must-draft list for their chances of bringing you a championship.

Fantasy points, rankings, average draft position (ADP) and other metrics courtesy of FantasyPros using PPR data unless noted.

The quarterback position isn't one that gets much focus in standard fantasy football leagues, but having an upper-echelon starter can make all the difference between a title run and missing the postseason entirely.

While addressing the position by drafting an established elite option such as Josh Allen (found on 16.3 percent of championship rosters) can shore the spot up with low risk, the opportunity cost of taking a QB that early can greatly hinder roster construction.

Considering three of the four other signal-callers found on ESPN's top-50 list of players on fantasy championship rosters last year didn't come off the board until pick No. 113 or later, it's clearly a position that managers can wait on and still succeed.

Managers who waited to select NFL MVP candidates Drake Maye (ADP 125.1) and Matt Stafford (ADP 159.9) last year were rewarded for their patience, and those who do the same with Malik Willis in 2026 could have similar results.

Willis has the makeup of a late-round quarterback who unexpectedly breaks out as a top-five fantasy performer. After two years working as the Green Bay Packers' backup, he's ready to take center stage as the Miami Dolphins' No. 1 option.

While Miami isn't expected to be a Super Bowl contender, the offense has plenty of potential. Willis' supporting cast includes an elite pass-catching running back in De'Von Achane, as well as a receiving corps that features fellow free-agent addition Jalen Tolbert, incumbent Malik Washington and a trio of promising rookies headlined by third-rounders Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell.

Willis has his biggest advantage on the ground, with dual-threat capabilities that can result in some massive fantasy outings. He rushed for 60 yards and two touchdowns on nine carries in his lone start of the 2025 season and racked up 73 yards and a score on just six totes in the last of two starts he made during the 2024 campaign.

Although he's far from a sure thing, Willis' lowly QB21 status and ADP of 167 make him the ideal late-round dice roll for managers who don't want to invest heavily into the QB position and still come away with the potential for an upper-echelon starter.

The Jacksonville Jaguars raised some eyebrows this offseason when they allowed star running back Travis Etienne Jr. to depart in free agency and failed to replace him with any notable free-agent or draft additions.

That decision signaled the club's faith in Bhayshul Tuten, the 2025 fourth-rounder who is set to open his sophomore season as Jacksonville's top RB.

While Tuten only saw sporadic work as a rookie and finished as the RB53 with a modest 88.6 points last year, he was efficient with his limited touches and flashed star potential.

In Week 2 against the Carolina Panthers—his first game as the primary backup to Etienne—he put up 74 yards and a touchdown on just 10 touches. He also had another top-20 finish later in the season, tallying 74 yards and a score on 15 carries in Week 11.

Tuten offers a rare blend of explosiveness, speed and power. He's not huge at 5'9", 209 pounds, but his compact frame has been difficult for defenders to bring down. Head coach Liam Coen brought these factors up during a recent interview on The Schrager Hour and projected a "big year" for the back:

Coen has a proven track record when it comes to maximizing the potential of his lead backs. Not only did the coach's system help Etienne finish as the RB10 last season—improving drastically from his RB35 ranking in 2024—but it also resulted in Bucky Irving unexpectedly exploding to an RB13 finish during Coen's lone season as the Tampa Bay Buccaneers' offensive coordinator two years ago.

There are valid concerns about Tuten's ball security issues and whether he'll be able to withstand the rigors of an NFL season as a full-time starter, but these aren't enough to justify skipping over a high-ceiling player.

Despite the elite talent and ample opportunities Tuten will have as Jacksonville's lead back, he's currently the RB23 with an ADP of 56. He has far more potential than most of his contemporaries in that range, making this a slam-dunk pick for managers willing to absorb a little risk in exchange for a possible league winner.

If Christian Watson can stay healthy, he will be one of the top-performing wide receivers in fantasy football this year. While injuries have been the unfortunate story of the Green Bay Packers wideout's career, that may finally change in 2026.

After going down with an ACL tear late in the 2024 season, he went on to miss nearly half the 2025 campaign whilst recovering. Although it took him a few weeks to shake off the rust and get back up to speed, the wideout began to make his presence felt late in the year.

He finished as the WR12 or better four times between Weeks 11-17, ending that stretch as the WR11 with an average of 15.1 points per game.

If Watson can pick up where he left off, he'll have few issues exceeding the expectations of a player being drafted No. 68 (WR30) on average. While he's missed 20 games since the Packers selected him early in the second round of the 2022 draft, the potential is far too enticing to pass over.

Watson made it through the offseason unscathed and is set to open the year as Green Bay's top wideout. It's a role that should be extremely fruitful, especially with quarterback Jordan Love looking poised to take a leap in his fourth season as the starter.

Watson is a home run threat every time he runs a route, using his combination of length, speed and hands to beat out defensive backs. Although he hasn't generated a ton of targets early in his career, that is on track to change with less competition for looks and with Love growing more comfortable as a passer.

The team may need to lean more heavily on its receiving corps with Josh Jacobs expected to miss an indefinite period .

With Watson healthy and ready to open 2026 in a feature role, Green Bay was able to clear the logjam that plagued its receiving corps in recent seasons.

These decisions, which included allowing 2025 top target-getter Romeo Doubs to walk in free agency and trading Dontayvion Wicks (third on the team in targets last year) to the Philadelphia Eagles, left Watson as the WR1 with Jayden Reed and Matthew Golden battling for looks behind him.

The Indianapolis Colts found a foundational tight end in last year's draft with Tyler Warren. The Penn State product had a strong rookie campaign—finishing as the TE4 with 188.5 points—and on average is the fourth TE off the board in 2026 fantasy drafts, but he's still being undervalued in relation to his potential production.

While Brock Bowers, Trey McBride and Colston Loveland all have the potential to put up massive numbers, the burgeoning Indianapolis superstar is the strongest bet to finish as the 2026 TE1.

Warren was on a torrid pace to open 2025, trailing only McBride for most points at the position over the first 10 weeks. He had four top-five weekly finishes and only placed outside the top-20 twice in that span, but struggled mightily after the team's Week 11 bye. Indy's offense, which had begun to falter when Daniel Jones broke his fibula, completely cratered after the starting QB went down with an Achilles injury in Week 14.

Had he averaged the same 13.6 points he was putting up during the first 10 weeks over the last seven contests, Warren would have finished as the TE2. Despite failing to finish inside the top-12 in any of the final seven games, Warren still had an overall solid first year and is set up nicely to build upon it.

Not only will Warren naturally improve as he gets more established and comfortable while growing his skill set in Year 2, but he's also set to benefit from some roster changes.

The 111 targets that Michael Pittman Jr. collected last year are up for grabs following his departure, while reigning target-leader Alec Pierce could also be less of a factor after he missed nearly an entire offseason while recovering from a nagging ankle issue.

It all sets up nicely for Warren to provide an incredible return on investment for those fantasy managers fortunate enough to land him near his current ADP of 51. If he paces his premium position by flirting with 300 points, managers will have a league winner on their hands.

Kickers in fantasy football have become controversial, with some leagues starting to remove the position due to a perceived lack of predictability.

Many still have a spot in the starting lineup designated for one, however, and for most players identifying a good kicker will remain an important way to get an edge in 2026.

Brandon Aubrey was the most commonly found kicker on last season's championship teams, but Jason Myers (13.5 percent rostered on title-winning squads) and Cameron Dicker (13 percent) were also game-changers for their managers.

Myers wasn't well-regarded heading into the campaign and went undrafted in most formats, but became the only kicker to breach the 200-point mark during his march to becoming the season's top-scoring kicker.

Will Lutz could follow in Myers' footsteps. While he currently sits in the middle of the pack as the K14—meaning he won't be selected in most 12-team leagues—he could quickly become a must-add weapon who can swing close games.

Lutz will benefit from being an integral part of a Denver Broncos squad that boasts a top-notch defense and a solid, but not great offense. This, along with the friendly home conditions in the Mile High, should lead Lutz to re-establish himself as one of the top fantasy kickers.

Although Lutz only finished as the K16 last year, he was a top-10 option as recently as the 2024 season. The nine-year veteran has a long history of production, having finished between K2 and K7 in every season from his 2016 rookie campaign through his 2019 Pro Bowl season.

Once you factor in Denver's softer schedule, Sean Payton's relatively conservative approach to fourth-down decisions and a steady offense that will move the ball into field-goal range with regularity, it's easy to see a path for Lutz's return to the NFL's upper tier.

articles.title: NFL Execs Sound Off on NFC's Top Teams in Poll Ahead of 2026 Season, Where Do Rams, Seahawks Rank?
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks are the reigning Super Bowl champions, but they're not the top dog in the NFC in the eyes of some NFL executives.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks are the reigning Super Bowl champions, but they're not the top dog in the NFC in the eyes of some NFL executives.

The Athletic's Mike Sando polled six execs, four of whom placed the Los Angeles Rams atop the conference. The Seahawks were second on the list, with one respondent putting them all the way in sixth.

One executive said a "clear gap" exists between the Rams and everyone else after three-time Defensive Player of the Year Aaron Donald ended his retirement.

A former general manager labeled L.A. "the best team in the NFC by far."

"Beyond all the defensive additions, Matthew Stafford is just surgical. So impressive," he said.

The Seahawks, meanwhile, had to replace offensive coordinator Klint Kubiak, and Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III left to sign with the Kansas City Chiefs.

"It is hard for me to think you're not going to have some kind of dropoff going from Kubiak to (Brian) Fleury, even if it is in the same schematic realm," one voter told Sando. "You lost Kubiak, you lost the Super Bowl MVP. I know you're excited about Jadarian Price, but …"

The Philadelphia Eagles, Dallas Cowboys and Chicago Bears rounded out the top five in the NFC.

The Bears are one of the conference's biggest wild cards. They went 11-6 and won the NFC North but finished with a plus-26 point differential. By comparison, the Detroit Lions were last in the division at 9-8 and had a plus-68 point differential.

Chicago won a lot of close games — Caleb Williams' six fourth-quarter comebacks were the most of any quarterback — and had the best turnover differential in the league. That's a difficult formula to replicate from one season to the next.

Williams may have another level to his game. If that's the case, then the Bears should not be playing from behind as much as they were in 2025.

One exec went so far as to rank Chicago first in the NFC. That kind of finish is within the realm of possibility. And so is the Bears missing the playoffs altogether.

articles.title: 49ers' Keion White Drops Viral Quote About Melatonin in Trending Video Ahead of Flight to Australia
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers defensive end Keion White is hoping that getting plenty of sleep will help him combat jet lag when the Niners travel to Australia for their season-opening game against the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
San Francisco 49ers defensive end Keion White is hoping that getting plenty of sleep will help him combat jet lag when the Niners travel to Australia for their season-opening game against the Los Angeles Rams.

Speaking to reporters Tuesday about his plan for the 15-hour flight, White said, "I don't know if you can OD on melatonin, but I'm gonna try. Take like five melatonin, go to sleep on the plane, as soon as I wake up, I'm taking five more."

On Sept. 10, the 49ers and Rams will meet in the first NFL regular-season game ever played in Australia at Melbourne Cricket Ground in Melbourne.
